jobs.excerpt: About TouchBistroTouchBistro is an all-in-one restaurant management platform built to help restaurant operators run stronger, more successful businesses.
jobs.description:
About TouchBistro

TouchBistro is an all-in-one restaurant management platform built to help restaurant operators run stronger, more successful businesses. Our solutions span point of sale, payments, front-of-house and back-of-house operations, and guest engagement. As part of Harris Computer, TouchBistro combines the focus and agility of a restaurant technology company with the long-term orientation of a leading vertical market software organization.


The Opportunity

TouchBistro is seeking an experienced Vice President, Sales & Marketing to lead an integrated go-to-market organization across North America. Reporting to the EVP, this executive will translate company strategy into a focused commercial plan, build a predictable and efficient revenue engine, sharpen our market position, and develop high-performing Sales and Marketing teams.

This is a hands-on executive role for a leader who can connect market insight, product value, demand generation, sales execution, pricing, brand, content, web, analytics, and marketing operations. The successful candidate will bring clarity to how TouchBistro targets the right customers, communicates differentiated value, creates and converts demand, and measures performance from first touch through booked and live recurring revenue.

What Success Looks Like

  • A clear, company-wide commercial strategy that defines priority markets, ideal customer profiles, channel choices, value propositions, and measurable growth outcomes.
  • A predictable funnel with disciplined forecasting, strong pipeline hygiene, clear stage definitions, and transparent conversion performance from lead through booking and activation handoff.
  • Improved sales and marketing efficiency, with investment decisions grounded in customer quality, unit economics, expected lifetime value, payback, and live recurring revenue.
  • Stronger product positioning, pricing discipline, launch execution, competitive intelligence, and sales enablement across the TouchBistro portfolio.
  • One integrated Sales and Marketing operating rhythm, with shared priorities, clear accountability, fast learning cycles, and a culture of coaching and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Growth Strategy & Leadership

  • Own the overall Sales and Marketing strategy and operating plan, aligned to TouchBistro’s business priorities, financial objectives, product roadmap, and customer strategy.
  • Translate growth objectives into market, segment, channel, capacity, investment, and talent plans with clear assumptions and measurable outcomes.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the Sales and Marketing leadership team; establish clear decision rights, performance expectations, succession plans, and career paths.
  • Create an integrated operating cadence across Sales and Marketing, including weekly execution reviews, monthly funnel and forecast reviews, and quarterly business planning.
  • Act as a key member of the executive leadership team, bringing a market- and customer-informed perspective to company strategy, resource allocation, and portfolio decisions.

Sales Strategy, Pipeline & Execution

  • Own delivery of new-business revenue targets and the commercial performance of inbound, outbound, and business development motions.
  • Build a disciplined, repeatable sales process covering lead response, qualification, discovery, demonstration, solution fit, proposal, negotiation, contracting, and close.
  • Establish consistent definitions and controls for pipeline creation, stage progression, conversion, forecast categories, sales-cycle velocity, win/loss analysis, and CRM hygiene.
  • Align account coverage, territories, quotas, capacity, and compensation with priority customer segments and expected demand.
  • Develop high-performing sales leaders and teams through structured onboarding, coaching, call review, playbooks, feedback, and clear career paths.
  • Partner with Customer Success and Operations to ensure honest expectations, clean handoffs, customer readiness, and stronger conversion from sold to live.
  • Provide executive sponsorship for strategic prospects, customers, RFPs, and complex commercial negotiations when appropriate.

Demand Generation & Revenue Marketing

  • Set the inbound and outbound demand generation strategy across paid search, SEO, lifecycle nurture, paid social, website, events, webinars, account-based programs, and other relevant channels.
  • Allocate budgets across markets, audiences, and channels based on pipeline contribution, customer quality, conversion, ACV, payback, and return on investment.
  • Build an experimentation roadmap to improve audience targeting, offer design, channel mix, lead quality, conversion, and speed to learning.
  • Create tight alignment between Marketing and Sales on campaign priorities, service-level expectations, lead routing, follow-up, qualification, and feedback loops.
  • Balance short-term pipeline creation with long-term category credibility, brand strength, customer advocacy, and organic demand.

Product Marketing, Pricing & Go-to-Market

  • Own the commercial articulation of TouchBistro’s value proposition, product positioning, messaging architecture, proof points, and differentiation by customer segment and use case.
  • Lead go-to-market planning and execution for new products, bundles, features, releases, and market entries in partnership with Product, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, and Operations.
  • Build a disciplined pricing and packaging capability informed by customer value, competitive dynamics, willingness to pay, margin, attach potential, and long-term unit economics.
  • Institutionalize market and competitive intelligence and translate insights into positioning, enablement, pricing, roadmap input, and commercial action.
  • Ensure Sales has the tools, training, battlecards, pricing guidance, customer stories, presentations, and collateral required to sell value consistently.

Brand, Content, Community & Communications

  • Define and protect TouchBistro’s brand strategy, voice, narrative, and standards across digital and traditional customer touchpoints.
  • Oversee an integrated content strategy spanning thought leadership, SEO and answer-engine visibility, product content, customer stories, newsletters, nurture, social media, events, podcasts, webinars, and sales collateral.
  • Ensure content is grounded in restaurant operator needs, product value, customer evidence, industry trends, and clear business objectives across the funnel.
  • Strengthen community engagement, customer advocacy, employee advocacy, and social listening while ensuring timely, consistent brand interaction.
  • Use research and original insights to build credibility in restaurant technology and create reusable demand, PR, sales, partner, and customer assets.

Digital Experience & Web

  • Treat the website and digital ecosystem as core commercial products that support discovery, education, conversion, and customer trust.
  • Own the web roadmap, conversion strategy, user journeys, landing-page effectiveness, accessibility, SEO foundations, performance, scalability, and content-management governance.
  • Use analytics, behavioral data, experimentation, and A/B testing to continuously improve digital conversion and campaign performance.
  • Ensure web development, design, content, product marketing, demand generation, and marketing operations work from shared priorities and measurable outcomes.
  • Oversee external agencies and vendors where needed, with clear scope, accountability, quality standards, and return expectations.

Marketing Operations, Data & Technology

  • Own marketing processes, automation, campaign operations, lead management, attribution, data quality, consent and governance, and the effectiveness of the marketing technology stack.
  • Ensure reliable integration between marketing platforms and CRM, with clear lifecycle definitions, routing, scoring, source tracking, and closed-loop reporting.
  • Develop dashboards that connect activity and spend to pipeline, booked ACV, live ACV, customer quality, payback, and retention-relevant indicators.
  • Create a trusted performance narrative by combining data with actionable insight, identifying root causes, and recommending clear management actions.
  • Simplify tools and workflows, automate repetitive work, and use AI responsibly to improve targeting, content operations, seller productivity, analysis, and speed of execution.

Cross-Functional Commercial Alignment

  • Partner closely with Product to bring customer and competitive insight into roadmap choices, business cases, packaging, launches, and lifecycle decisions.
  • Partner with Finance on targets, budgets, forecast assumptions, unit economics, deal quality, pricing governance, and investment trade-offs.
  • Partner with Customer Success and Operations to improve sales-to-activation handoffs, surface expectation gaps, support retention, and create customer expansion and advocacy opportunities.
  • Build strong relationships with strategic customers and ecosystem partners and represent TouchBistro at relevant industry events and executive forums.
  • Promote direct communication, clear ownership, and shared metrics across the full customer journey.

Performance Management

The VP will establish a concise executive scorecard and use it to drive decisions, accountability, and continuous improvement. Measures are expected to include:


Growth : Booked ACV, live ACV, new recurring revenue, average deal size, attainment by channel and segment

Funnel : Pipeline coverage, lead-to-opportunity conversion, win rate, sales-cycle velocity, forecast accuracy

Efficiency : Sales and Marketing spend to live ACV, CAC and payback, channel ROI, quota capacity and productivity

Customer quality : Ideal-customer mix, sold-to-kickoff and sold-to-live conversion, early-life churn indicators, expectation quality

Marketing : Qualified pipeline contribution, website conversion, content and nurture influence, attribution quality, brand and share-of-voice indicators

Execution : CRM hygiene, speed to lead, campaign delivery, launch readiness, pricing compliance, enablement adoption

People : Engagement, retention, leadership bench strength, ramp time, coaching effectiveness, succession coverage

Qualifications & Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive commercial leadership experience across Sales, Marketing, business development, revenue growth, or related functions, including significant leadership-of-leaders responsibility.
  • Proven success leading an integrated go-to-market organization in B2B SaaS, vertical market software, payments, restaurant technology, hospitality technology, or a comparable high-volume commercial environment.
  • Demonstrated accountability for revenue targets, demand generation, pipeline management, forecasting, pricing, budgets, and commercial performance.
  • Strong command of SaaS unit economics, funnel analytics, attribution, customer acquisition, payback, retention dynamics, and investment trade-offs.
  • Experience building disciplined sales processes and coaching teams across inbound, outbound, transactional, and complex sales motions.
  • Experience leading product marketing, positioning, messaging, go-to-market launches, pricing and packaging, competitive intelligence, and sales enablement.
  • Working knowledge of modern marketing operations, CRM, automation, analytics, web conversion, content, SEO, lifecycle marketing, and AI-enabled workflows.
  • Strong executive presence, commercial judgment, negotiation skills, and the ability to communicate clearly with employees, customers, partners, and senior stakeholders.
  • A builder’s mindset: strategic enough to set direction, analytical enough to challenge assumptions, and hands-on enough to improve execution.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Commerce, or a related field; equivalent experience will be considered. MBA is an asset.
  • Restaurant, hospitality, POS, payments, or multi-location software experience is a strong asset.
  • English required; French is a strong asset for the Canadian market. Ability to travel within North America as required.

Leadership Profile

Commercially rigorous : Makes allocation and pricing decisions using evidence, unit economics, and customer value.

Customer-centered : Understands restaurant operators and insists that promises, products, and delivery stay aligned.

Clear and accountable : Sets a small number of priorities, assigns ownership, and addresses gaps directly and constructively.

Integrated thinker : Connects brand, product, demand, sales, activation, retention, and expansion rather than optimizing silos.

Talent builder : Develops leaders, raises the performance bar, and creates a coaching culture with visible career paths.

Adaptive operator : Tests, learns, and changes course quickly without sacrificing standards, data quality, or customer trust.

What We Offer

  • A high-impact executive mandate with direct influence on TouchBistro’s growth strategy and operating model.
  • The opportunity to lead an established Sales and Marketing organization through its next stage of focus, integration, and performance.
  • A collaborative environment with access to the broader Harris Computer network and long-term operating perspective.
  • Flexible work arrangements, competitive executive compensation with performance-based incentives, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Salary range: $120,000–$150,000 CAD annually, depending on experience.

Application & Equal Opportunity

*Only selected candidates will be contacted.

Harris is committed to an equal employment opportunity program, and applications from members of designated groups, including women, persons with disabilities, Indigenous peoples, and visible minorities, are encouraged. If you are a person with a disability, you may request assistance with the recruitment and selection process.

Harris’s Talent Acquisition team does not use text messages to communicate with candidates or to solicit confidential information. Candidates will be contacted either by a Harris manager or a member of the Talent Acquisition team for an interview, provided they meet the required qualifications.

jobs.title: Financial Analyst - Accounting & Advisory
jobs.excerpt: About the ClientWe’re helping a boutique professional services and advisory firm based in Nassau, The Bahamas find a Financial Analyst to support its growing portfolio of clients.
jobs.description:
About the Client

We’re helping a boutique professional services and advisory firm based in Nassau, The Bahamas find a Financial Analyst to support its growing portfolio of clients.

The firm works with entrepreneurs, established businesses, institutions, and international clients across strategic and financial advisory, corporate services, accounting and bookkeeping, back-office administration, and project management. Its clients span a variety of industries, including healthcare, professional services, government, and other service-based businesses.

The Role

We’re looking for a Financial Analyst – Accounting & Advisory to support the financial reporting, analysis, and research that underpin the firm's strategic advisory work.

The role sits at the intersection of accounting operations, financial analysis, and advisory support. You’ll work across multiple client businesses, preparing and analyzing P&Ls, balance sheets, cash flow statements, monthly financial packs, and straightforward forecasts while ensuring the senior advisory team has accurate and well-structured financial information to work from.

This is not primarily a valuation or complex financial modeling role. Instead, you'll develop a strong understanding of the financial operations of different businesses and turn their numbers into useful insights and structured outputs that support strategic decision-making.

There may also be research, commercial analysis, and project work depending on the needs of each client. As you develop, there is an opportunity to become increasingly involved in the strategic advisory side of the business.

Role Details

Commitment: Full-Time (40 hours/week)

Working Hours: Bahamas working hours

Location: Fully Remote

Engagement: Independent Contractor

Start Date: ASAP

Monthly Rate: $1,800-$2,400 (can be higher, depending on level of experience)

What You’ll Do

Financial Reporting & Accounting Support

  • Prepare and maintain P&Ls, balance sheets, cash flow statements, and other financial reports across multiple client accounts.

  • Prepare recurring monthly financial and management reporting packs using established templates and processes.

  • Review and organize financial information to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency.

  • Analyze financial performance and identify relevant trends, movements, discrepancies, and areas requiring attention.

  • Support the financial back-office requirements of non-finance businesses across different industries.

  • Maintain well-organized financial information and supporting documentation across client accounts.

  • Learn and work with client-specific accounting systems, processes, and proprietary software where required.

Forecasting & Financial Analysis

  • Prepare and maintain straightforward financial forecasts and projections.

  • Support cash flow planning and other forward-looking financial analysis.

  • Analyze historical and current financial performance to help inform business decisions.

  • Assist with financial analysis relating to commercial credit, loan financing, and other business requirements where needed.

  • Translate financial data into clear and structured information for senior team members.

  • Flag unusual movements, inconsistencies, or areas that warrant further investigation.

The modeling requirements for this role are relatively straightforward. You won't be expected to build complex valuation or transaction models; the emphasis is on strong financial fundamentals, accurate reporting, practical forecasting, and understanding what the numbers mean for the business.

Strategic Advisory & Research Support

  • Prepare financial information and analysis used by senior team members in client-facing strategic advisory work.

  • Conduct business, financial, market, or industry research where required for client assignments.

  • Gather and structure information needed to support strategic recommendations.

  • Help turn financial and research findings into clear reports, presentations, and other client-facing materials.

  • Support senior team members with ad hoc analysis for different business challenges and opportunities.

  • Develop an understanding of each client's business model, operations, and commercial environment rather than looking at financial information in isolation.

Client & Project Support

  • Work across multiple client accounts and adapt to different industries, business models, and reporting requirements.

  • Support project coordination, documentation, and follow-up across advisory engagements.

  • Manage recurring deliverables and ensure financial information is prepared accurately and on time.

  • Assist with broader analytical and administrative requirements connected to client projects.

  • Take increasing ownership of client work as your understanding and capabilities develop.

What We’re Looking For

Must-Haves

  • Ideally 3–5 years of relevant experience in financial analysis, accounting, FP&A, management reporting, corporate services, or a similar finance-focused environment. However, practical capability is more important to us than a specific number of years.

  • Academic background in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field.

  • Strong understanding of P&Ls, balance sheets, and cash flow statements and how they work together.

  • Hands-on experience preparing and analyzing financial reports and management information.

  • Comfortable preparing straightforward forecasts and financial projections.

  • Strong numerical, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills and confidence working with financial data.

  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

  • Ability to identify trends, inconsistencies, and relevant insights from financial information.

  • Ability to work across multiple clients, assignments, and deadlines.

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to learn new systems and processes quickly.

  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills.

  • Ability to work independently, take ownership of deliverables, and recognize when issues need to be escalated.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience in professional services, corporate consultancy, accounting, FP&A, or financial advisory.

  • Experience supporting multiple external client accounts.

  • Experience working with SMEs or service-based businesses.

  • Exposure to healthcare, medical, dental, government, or other professional-services clients.

  • Understanding of commercial lending, loan financing, or credit analysis.

  • Experience preparing management reports and financial projections.

  • Previous exposure to strategic advisory or consulting projects.

  • Experience conducting business, market, or industry research.

  • Experience managing or supporting financial back-office operations for non-finance businesses.

  • Experience working across multiple industries.

Ideal Candidate Profile

You’re someone who is strong with numbers but also interested in the business behind them.

You can confidently work with P&Ls, balance sheets, and cash flows, prepare reliable financial reporting, maintain forecasts, and spot when something doesn’t look right. At the same time, you’re curious about why the numbers are moving and what they mean for the business.

You may come from accounting, FP&A, financial analysis, consulting, or even a more traditional financial analyst background. What matters most is that you're comfortable with the practical financial work involved and genuinely interested in supporting businesses across a range of financial and strategic challenges.

This could also be a good fit for someone with a more modeling- or transaction-oriented finance background who is looking to move into a role with less emphasis on complex modeling and transactions and greater exposure to ongoing business operations and strategic advisory.

You’re organized, adaptable, commercially curious, and comfortable switching between financial reporting, forecasting, research, and project work across different client engagements.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means becoming a reliable extension of the advisory team who can independently manage high-quality financial preparation and analysis across multiple clients.

You’ll progressively reduce the financial preparation required from senior team members by ensuring reports, financial packs, forecasts, research, and supporting information are accurate, well-structured, and ready for use in strategic discussions.

As your understanding of the clients and advisory work develops, there will be opportunities to take on greater responsibility across financial analysis, research, strategic advisory, and project support.

Why Join?

  • Gain exposure to the financial operations and strategic challenges of multiple businesses and industries.

  • Work closely with experienced professionals on real-world client advisory engagements.

  • Build experience beyond traditional accounting or financial reporting into research and strategic advisory.

  • Take meaningful ownership of client work rather than being limited to one narrow finance function.

  • Develop a broader understanding of how financial information supports business strategy and decision-making.

  • Opportunity to grow into greater advisory and project responsibilities over time.

  • Join a fully remote team with a long-term opportunity for professional development.

Recruitment Process

  1. Initial Interview with Bamboo Works

  2. Client Interview

  3. Practical Financial Assessment for Finalists

  4. Offer & Onboarding

The practical assessment will take place after the client interview stage and will only be completed by final shortlisted candidates.

jobs.description:
Location:Abidjan, Côte I'voire or Dakar, Senegal

About Djamo

Djamo is a Series B neobank serving over 1 million customers across Francophone Africa. We're the first fintech to receive a BCEAO microfinance license and the leading card issuer in Côte d'Ivoire. Our engineering team is 27 strong, organized into cross-functional squads that own end-to-end product experiences, from virtual cards and transactions to savings, credit, and customer support.

We're growing fast, but we're deliberate about how. We care about reliability, security, and shipping things that actually work for our customers.

Why this role exists

We're a bank. Security isn't optional, it's existential. Today we rely on external vendors for penetration testing across four scopes: our Dakar office, Abidjan office, cloud infrastructure, and applications.

We need an in-house penetration tester who knows Djamo deeply, can test continuously rather than annually, and becomes a true security partner to our engineering teams. This hire saves money from year one while dramatically improving our security posture.

What you'll do

  • Plan and execute penetration tests across all four scopes: office networks (Dakar, Abidjan), cloud infrastructure (AWS), and applications (web + mobile).
  • Conduct regular vulnerability assessments and produce clear, actionable reports for engineering teams.
  • Work with engineering squads to verify fixes and retest after remediation.
  • Contribute to Djamo's security posture by identifying systemic weaknesses, not just individual vulnerabilities.
  • Support PCI DSS compliance by providing evidence of regular security testing.
  • Stay current on emerging threats and attack techniques relevant to fintech and banking.
  • Travel periodically to Abidjan and Dakar offices for on-site network and physical security assessments.

What we're looking for

Must have:

  • 3+ years of hands-on penetration testing experience.
  • Strong web application and API security testing skills (OWASP Top 10 and beyond).
  • Network penetration testing experience (internal and external).
  • Experience with common pen testing tools: Burp Suite, Nmap, Metasploit, Nessus/OpenVAS, etc.
  • Ability to write clear, prioritized vulnerability reports that engineering teams can act on.
  • Clear communication in English: written and verbal.
  • Willingness to travel periodically between Dakar and Abidjan.

Strong plus:

  • OSCP, OSCE, OSWE, or equivalent certification.
  • CEH, GPEN, or other recognized security certifications.
  • Mobile application security testing (Android/iOS).
  • Cloud security assessment experience (AWS).
  • Experience in fintech, banking, or PCI DSS-regulated environments.
  • French-speaking.
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code security review (Terraform, Kubernetes).

What we're NOT looking for:

  • Someone who runs automated scanners and calls it a pen test. We need manual testing depth.
  • A researcher who can find vulnerabilities but can't communicate them clearly to developers.

What success looks like after 6 months

  • You've completed a full cycle of pen tests across all four scopes.
  • Engineering teams trust your reports and act on them promptly.
  • We've reduced or eliminated our dependency on external pen test vendors.
  • You've identified and helped remediate systemic security issues, not just surface-level findings.
  • You have a testing calendar that ensures continuous coverage rather than annual point-in-time assessments.

How we work

  • Remote-first, asynchronous by default.
  • Small engineering team (27 engineers) your impact will be visible and immediate.
  • We take reliability and security seriously: we're a bank, not a social app.
  • You'll work closely with the ISSM, engineering squads, and infrastructure team.

Why work at Djamo

  • Balance between autonomy and collaboration, insight and intuition, work and life.
  • Work in small, open, friendly teams to create beloved products and services.
  • Ethical and stimulating environment.
  • Contribute to the rapid expansion of a startup in French-speaking Africa.
  • Positively impact millions by providing simple and fair banking.
  • Collaborative, fun environment with strong team spirit and a culture of continuous employee development.

We will consider all applications on the same basis. Djamo is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. You are not ticking every box or thinking you've got that unique set of skills we haven't realized we need. Apply anyway; we're always looking to add great people at every level.

jobs.description:
As a Social Media Manager at vCluster, you aren't just scheduling posts—you are building the technical voice of one of the most interesting infrastructure companies in the cloud-native ecosystem. You will own the full social program across LinkedIn and X, turn the thinking of our leaders into content the Kubernetes community actually wants to read, and show up live at the events that matter most to our audience.

What You’ll Do

  • Content Calendar Ownership: Plan, write, and publish weekly posts on LinkedIn and X. Stay two weeks ahead at all times. No gaps, no scramble.

  • Executive Thought Leadership Extraction: Turn the deep architectural insights of our leadership team into high-impact published content and thought leadership.

  • Community Management: Respond thoughtfully to comments, DMs, and mentions on both platforms. Engage with practitioners, contributors, and platform engineering leaders—adding real value to the infrastructure conversation, not just reacting.

  • Reactive Distribution: When something happens in the cloud-native and AI infra world—a major CNCF release, an architectural debate, a KubeCon announcement—you move fast to capture attention while the narrative has a short half-life.

  • Live Event Coverage: Cover priority global events (such as KubeCon and key AI Infra summits) in real time—delivering live threads on X, daily LinkedIn updates, and post-event structural recaps.

  • Editorial Quality Bar: Act as the standard-bearer for what goes out under our brand name. You will be expected to ruthlessly protect our brand voice, push back on subpar content, and actively propose higher-impact alternatives.

This Role is a Fit for You If:

  • Infrastructure Literacy: You don't need to be a Kubernetes kernel engineer, but you must be "infrastructure-literate." You understand the landscape well enough to write credibly for DevOps and platform teams.

  • Platform Mastery: You have an opinionated view on how to win on LinkedIn and X. You can point directly to developer-centric or highly technical social accounts you have personally scaled and grown.

  • Calendar Discipline: You operate with a clear structural framework. You build and own a structured content calendar without being asked, maintaining a two-week safety buffer by default.

  • Speed and Judgment: You balance high-velocity output with corporate judgment. You know exactly when to capitalize on an infrastructure trend instantly and when a narrative requires strict message alignment first.

  • Analytical Rigor: You measure social success by its ability to spark genuine community conversation, traffic, and distribution momentum—not just empty vanity metrics.

Bonus Points For:

  • Infrastructure Roots: Background managing social channels for developer tools, open-source ecosystems, or AI/MLOps infrastructure.

  • Executive Ghost-Writing: Direct experience translating deep technical expertise from executives into compelling, human narratives.

  • Multimedia Capability: Basic video clip selection and editing skills to transform live product demos or executive sessions into high-engagement social cuts.

  • On-Site Autonomy: Comfort being on-the-ground at massive industry events, executing a live social playbook entirely independently.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Platinum-Level Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

Compensation Range: $105K - $125K

jobs.title: Client Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Sentinel Blue is hiring a Client Engineer for our Operations team.
jobs.description:
Sentinel Blue is hiring a Client Engineer for our Operations team. This role is a senior, client-facing engineer who serves as a trusted technology advisor across Sentinel Blue’s client portfolio. This role sits within the Operations team and is built for an engineer who can operate at both the strategic and technical level. The perfect candidate is someone who can assess a client’s environment, understand their goals and constraints, and provide clear, actionable direction.

This is not a pure advisory role. You will be reviewing and modifying configurations, evaluating vendor proposals, identifying security and compliance implications, and producing documentation clients can act on. You will also collaborate internally to connect client needs to the right delivery teams or external partners.

This is a full-time position that is fully remote.

This position may require access to technology, technical data, or information that is subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations. Employment in this position is contingent upon either verification of U.S. person status as defined under applicable export control regulations (which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and certain protected individuals such as refugees and asylees) or the ability to obtain any required export authorization. The company reserves the right not to apply for an export license and to decline to proceed with any applicant on that basis. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to citizenship status, national origin, or immigration status.

A day in the Client Engineer role:

You might open a conversation with a client who wants to evaluate a new business intelligence platform. You'll work through what they're trying to accomplish, assess the hosting and infrastructure implications, identify where it touches identity or compliance, and produce a structured recommendation even if Sentinel Blue won't own the full implementation. That same week, you might be standing up the server infrastructure to host it, working through a configuration issue blocking a data connection, or troubleshooting why an integration with their identity provider isn't behaving as expected. Later, you're on a call reviewing a vendor proposal with a client's leadership team, helping them understand what questions to ask and what commitments to require. By end of day, you're translating that conversation into a written brief the client can take into their next board discussion.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the senior technology point of contact for assigned clients, owning the relationship at the strategic level.
  • Lead discovery conversations to understand client business goals, existing technology investments, and emerging needs.
  • Translate complex technical topics into clear guidance appropriate for non-technical stakeholders and executive audiences.
  • Represent Sentinel Blue on client calls with credibility, clarity, and a consultative approach.
  • Engage clients on technology requests and questions that fall outside standard managed service scope, including specialized platforms, line-of-business applications, and bespoke infrastructure needs.
  • Assess unfamiliar systems and platforms quickly, understanding hosting requirements, integration dependencies, security posture, and compliance implications even without deep prior experience with the specific tool.
  • Deploy, configure, and troubleshoot infrastructure and applications as part of client engagements, including standing up servers, modifying system configurations, and resolving application-level issues.
  • Provide guidance aligned with CMMC, NIST 800-171, and CIS Controls as applicable to client context.
  • Identify gaps, risks, and remediation priorities across client environments and communicate them clearly.
  • Help clients evaluate vendor proposals and technology investments, including RFP support, contract review from a technical lens, and total cost of ownership analysis.
  • Assess vendor security posture, SLA commitments, and integration readiness in the context of the client's environment.
  • Produce clear client-facing deliverables including assessments, roadmaps, briefing documents, and recommendation reports.
  • Collaborate with internal IT Operations, SOC, and GRC teams to route client needs to the right delivery function.
  • Contribute to internal knowledge by documenting patterns, assessments, and guidance for recurring client scenarios.

What We Can Offer:

Sentinel Blue is a young company with a focused mission: We’re bringing enterprise-class cybersecurity to small and medium sized businesses. Frankly, we’re pushing the envelope of how things are done and constantly seeking innovative ways to meet that mission. The pace is fast, and we’re always learning new things. This is a great place if you want to expose yourself to new and emerging technologies, want to be challenged, and want to build your skills. Further, success in this role can quickly transition into a senior engineering, architectural, or technical leadership role. The right person will find themselves in a fun, dynamic environment, working on interesting problems and making a real difference.

You will be required to achieve a Security+ certification in the first 6 months of hire; we’ll cover your certification costs and provide paid time for you to study!

Requirements:

  • 5–8 years of relevant experience in cloud infrastructure, IT consulting, or technology advisory roles with demonstrated client-facing ownership.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft 365, Azure, Entra ID, and modern identity and endpoint management.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess unfamiliar technology platforms and produce actionable recommendations without requiring end-to-end ownership of the system.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief executive and non-technical audiences clearly and confidently.
  • Troubleshooting skills and follow-through, including validation and documentation.
  • Experience engaging with compliance frameworks such as CMMC, NIST 800-171, or CIS Controls in a practical engineering or advisory context.
  • CompTIA Security+ required within 6 months of hire if not already held.

Desired Qualifications:

  • MSP, MSSP, or consulting background with responsibility across multiple client environments.
  • Hands-on experience in Azure Government, Microsoft 365 GCC High, or other FedRAMP Moderate environments.
  • Familiarity with vendor evaluation, RFP processes, and technology procurement advisory.
  • Experience assessing line-of-business or specialized applications (e.g., BI platforms, ERP/CRM systems, industry-specific tools) from an infrastructure, security, or compliance lens.
  • Proficiency in core networking fundamentals and practical exposure to platforms such as Fortinet, Meraki, Ubiquiti UniFi, or Cloudflare Zero Trust.
  • Familiarity with backup, recovery, and data retention concepts in cloud environments.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, or a related field.

Benefits:

  • Fully paid individual healthcare, vision and dental insurance for the employee.
  • Paid certification and training opportunities.
  • Three weeks of paid vacation + 10 paid holidays.
  • A supportive environment with a focus on keeping healthy work-life balance.
  • Retirement benefit (401k) with company match
Salary: $120,000 – $160,000 / year

You will also be responsible for maintaining high technical standards, managing team bandwidth, and ensuring project milestones are met with efficiency and accuracy.

  • Ensure robust monitoring, alerting, and observability for all owned services, consistently meeting defined SLIs and SLOs.
  • Partner with Product Managers to define, track, and publish post-release product metrics, driving transparency and continuous improvement.

To succeed in this role, you should have

  • 8-10 years of experience as a Software Developer, Software Engineer, or in a similar hands-on technical role.
  • 5+ years of strong experience building production systems using Java and Spring Boot.
  • Minimum 3 years of proven engineering leadership experience managing high-performing teams.
  • Solid grasp of Agile methodologies, including sprint planning, backlog grooming, and iterative delivery.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex product requirements into well-structured EPICs, user stories, and tasks.
  • Strong backend engineering expertise; exposure to frontend technologies is a plus.
  • Experience with project planning and tracking tools to visualize and manage delivery timelines.
  • Familiarity with engineering, product health metrics, and monitoring tools to drive data-informed decisions.
  • Hands-on capability to debug complex production issues, lead incident response, and conduct blameless RCA.
  • Good understanding of modern deployment practices, including CI/CD pipelines, release management, and associated metrics.
  • Ability to drive alignment across cross-functional stakeholders, both technical and non-technical.
  • Excellent risk management, dependency tracking, and stakeholder communication skills.
  • Proven track record of improving team velocity, delivery predictability, and engineering excellence.

Generic Skills

  • Problem-solving: Ability to assess complex problems, find solutions, and make sound decisions.
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, including technical documentation and stakeholder reporting.
  • Adaptability: Able to thrive in a fast-paced, changing environment, adjusting strategies as needed.
  • Attention to Detail: Meticulous in documenting technical requirements and ensuring all aspects of a project are accounted for.

Supervisory skills

  • Team Management: Experience in managing and mentoring engineers, ensuring team growth and performance.
  • Resource Allocation: Ability to assess bandwidth and manage resource distribution to optimize team performance.
  • Feedback: Conduct regular performance reviews, providing constructive feedback and fostering a growth-oriented environment.

jobs.excerpt: Job Overview: As a Red Hat Ansible Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and managing the company's automated system configuration and deployment strategies using Red Hat's Ansible.
jobs.description:
Job Overview:

As a Red Hat Ansible Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and managing the company's automated system configuration and deployment strategies using Red Hat's Ansible. You will work closely with system administrators, developers, and IT management to automate a wide range of tasks, from system setup and software deployment to network configuration and data management.

Key Responsibilities:

Automation Strategy Design & Implementation: Design and implement an automation strategy for the organization's IT systems using Ansible. This includes writing Ansible playbooks, setting up Ansible Tower, and integrating Ansible with other tools and platforms.

Configuration Management: Use Ansible to manage the configuration of servers, networks, and software across the organization. Ensure that all configurations meet the organization's standards and policies.

Software Deployment Automation: Use Ansible to automate the deployment of software across various environments. Work closely with development teams to integrate Ansible into the software development and deployment lifecycle.

System Troubleshooting & Support: Troubleshoot and resolve issues with the Ansible environment and automated tasks. Provide technical support to IT staff and users as needed.

Security & Compliance: Ensure that the use of Ansible and the configurations it manages comply with the organization's security policies and any relevant regulations. Use Ansible to automate security-related tasks such as patch deployment and system hardening.

Documentation & Reporting: Document all Ansible configurations, playbooks, and procedures. Prepare regular reports on system performance, availability, and compliance.

Training & Mentoring: Train and mentor other IT staff in the use of Ansible and the principles of IT automation. Promote the use of automation across the organization.

Requirements:

Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field. Professional certifications such as Red Hat Certified Engineer (RHCE) or Red Hat Certified Specialist in Ansible Automation are highly desirable.

Experience: At least 5 years of experience in IT, with at least 3 years of experience in managing Ansible environments.

Technical Skills: Strong understanding of Ansible and its components, including playbooks, roles, and Ansible Tower. Familiarity with Linux system administration, shell scripting, networking, and security. Experience with other configuration management or IT automation tools is a plus.

Soft Skills: Excellent problem-solving abilities, attention to detail, and communication skills. Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Physical Requirements: Depending on the specific role and location, this may involve working in a data center environment and handling heavy equipment.

Other: Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation and to travel, as needed.

Disclaimer:

This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skills, efforts, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position. The company is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.

jobs.excerpt: Champion AI is the strategic future of QAD | Redzone, and we are building a dedicated AI division to own it — this is where the company’s attention, investment, and ambition are concentrated.
jobs.description:
Champion AI is the strategic future of QAD | Redzone, and we are building a dedicated AI division to own it — this is where the company’s attention, investment, and ambition are concentrated. The strategy and the technical foundation are built; we need solution designers who can execute it and scale it across customers.

There has never been a better moment to sit at the frontier of agentic AI for manufacturing. We are assembling a small team of operators to capture it, and this role helps define what “great” looks like.

The Role

The AI Account Executive & Sales Solutions Engineer is a solution designer. You walk into a customer conversation, understand their end-to-end process, and assemble an agentic solution to fix it — without engineering involvement.

You sit on top of a pre-built foundation — data, semantics, an agent platform, and a library of persona agents. You configure within it; you don’t build it. The platform exposes configuration through natural language and drag-and-drop, so your edge is domain fluency and solution-design instinct, not code.

What You’ll Do

Working hand-in-hand with other Account Executives, you take a qualified opportunity and turn it into a working agentic solution:

  • Run process discovery workshops: sit with champion users to map any of the standard enterprise processes (P2P, S2C, O2C, P2M, F2P, R2R) — current state, KPIs, manual effort, bottlenecks, and target state.
  • Design the agentic solution: decide which agents, working together, fix the customer’s process — and recognize whether it’s a greenfield build or a brownfield plug-in to an existing system (SAP, Ariba, Coupa, Jaggaer).
  • Map KPIs to the platform: confirm the system has the data and the business context to measure what the customer actually cares about.
  • Configure each agent: set triggers, decision logic, exceptions, KPIs, data sources, communications, company-specific rules, and hand-offs — all in natural language and drag-and-drop, no code.
  • Present the solution: pitch anchored in business outcomes — OTIF, working capital, cycle time, cost reduction — worked backwards to the agents that achieve them.
  • You are a quota carrier with 3 or more years of experience selling Tech/AI/SaaS solutions.
  • Enterprise domain fluency: operational, end-to-end working knowledge of at least two of P2P, S2C, O2C, P2M, F2P, R2R — not just a consulting view. The deepest value sits in plan-to-make and procure-to-pay.
  • Solution-design thinking: ability to decompose a vague business outcome into agents and data flows, and to know when one agent suffices and when several are needed.
  • Low-code / natural-language comfort: hands-on with tools like n8n, Zapier, or Make. The agent platform will feel familiar.
  • Customer-facing credibility: workshop facilitation and executive-level presentation.

Nice-to-Have

  • Background at a major ERP vendor or process consultancy (SAP, Oracle, Coupa, Ariba, or a Big Four firm).
  • Hands-on experience with AI tooling.
  • Industry depth in manufacturing, particularly tier-one suppliers.

Not Required

Model-building, software-engineering depth, or an ML / data-science background. Engineering owns the platform; you own the solution.

Who Thrives Here

  • You are joining a small, entrepreneurial team — not a delivery machine with a ticket queue. We want self-starters who see the opportunity in agentic AI and move without waiting for instructions.
  • Self-starter: if a solution pattern or workshop framework doesn’t exist yet, you create it. If a document is missing, you write it.
  • Resourceful: you pull in the right people — your AE, Product, and Customer Success — to move a deal forward and get the customer to value.
  • Builder’s mindset: you take a strong foundation and a playbook and extend them as the platform matures, rather than waiting for every process to be defined for you.
  • If you need rigid structure and a clearly defined process for every situation, this is not the right place. If you want to shape how this role and this division are built, it is.
  • Compensation. $100,000— 140,000 USD ,
  • Plus a strong benefits package inclusive of PTO, 401K matching, and Healthcare/Medical Insurance plans.
  • Virtual-First Culture: work remotely, with the flexibility to lead in-person customer workshops in your market.
  • Atmosphere of Growth: join a team where idea-sharing is prioritized over hierarchy, at the leading edge of agentic AI for manufacturing.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: health, dental, vision, PTO, 401K matching, and a collaborative culture of smart, hard-working people.

About QAD:

QAD | Redzone is redefining manufacturing and supply chains through its intelligent, adaptive platform that connects people, processes, and data into a single System of Action. With three core pillars — Redzone (frontline empowerment), Adaptive Applications (the intelligent backbone), and Champion AI (Agentic AI for manufacturing) — QAD | Redzone helps manufacturers operate with Champion Pace, achieving measurable productivity, resilience, and growth in just 90 days.

QAD is committed to ensuring that every employee feels they work in an environment that values their contributions, respects their unique perspectives and provides opportunities for growth regardless of background. QAD’s DEI program is driving higher levels of diversity, equity and inclusion so that employees can bring their whole self to work.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

jobs.description:
Role Title: Physics Expert (Statistical Physics / Quantum Information / Condensed Matter)

Role Type: Part-Time, Contractor

Location: Fully Remote, Open to candidates worlwide

Schedule: 5-10+ hrs/week. Fully flexible (Can accomodate after hours + weekends if needed)

micro1 is engaging Physics Experts (Statistical Physics / Quantum Information / Condensed Matter) to contribute to a research-driven customer project at the intersection of theoretical physics and numerical benchmarking.

In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Analyze and provide expert insights into complex statistical physics phenomena, with a focus on replicated random-bond Ising/Ashkin-Teller models, the toric-code threshold, and the Nishimori line.
  2. Deliver clear, well-documented solutions or critiques of problems relating to Kramers-Wannier duality, quenched disorder averaging, square-lattice self-duality, and domain-wall free energy.
  3. Engage in advanced numerical work, particularly around 4-state Potts model simulations and interpretation.
  4. Identify, discuss, and resolve technical challenges involving noncontractible loop defects and related topological features.
  5. Participate as a Solver, Auditor, or Adjudicator on specific project assignments based on your experience and subfield strengths.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Advanced academic background (PhD or equivalent experience) in physics, with specialization in statistical physics, quantum information, or condensed matter theory.
  2. Direct, hands-on experience applying Kramers-Wannier duality, quenched disorder averaging, and square-lattice self-duality in research or project settings.
  3. Demonstrated proficiency in numerical simulations involving the 4-state Potts model and analysis of domain-wall free energy.
  4. Familiarity with topological quantum codes, particularly the toric code and its threshold phenomena.

Start: ab sofort | Level: Senior | Location: Deutschland, remote | Arbeitszeit: Vollzeit (40h/Woche)

Als IT Security Architekt (gn) – IAM & OnPrem verantwortest du das Sicherheits-Zielbild und die Standards für Identitäten und die On-Premises-Infrastruktur. Du entwirfst Referenzarchitekturen für Identity & Access Management, On-Prem Active Directory (inkl. hybrider Anbindung an Entra ID) sowie die zugehörige On-Prem-Infrastruktur und berätst die umsetzenden Teams. Die operative Umsetzung liegt bei den Fachteams; dein Beitrag ist Design, Standardsetzung und fachliche Beratung.

Deine Mission bei uns

  • Verantwortungsbereiche / Domänen

    • Identity & Access Management (IAM): Referenzarchitektur und Standards für Rollen- und Berechtigungskonzepte, Rezertifizierung, Joiner/Mover/Leaver-Prozesse und privilegierte Zugriffe (PAM).
    • On-Prem Active Directory: Härtungs- und Tiering-Konzepte, Absicherung privilegierter Konten, sichere Administrationsmodelle.
    • Entra ID (Hybrid): Sichere Kopplung von On-Prem AD und Cloud-Identität, Conditional Access, Privileged Identity Management – als Teil eines konsistenten hybriden Identitätskonzepts.
    • On-Prem Infrastruktur & Netzwerk: Sicherheitsvorgaben für Segmentierung, Zugriffs- und Übergangsarchitekturen sowie sichere Fernzugriffe im On-Prem-Umfeld.
    • OT / Produktionssicherheit (optional, zukünftig): Vorgesehen als zukünftige Erweiterung des Verantwortungsbereichs – Referenzarchitektur und Standards für die sichere Trennung und Anbindung von OT-/Produktionssystemen (Standort Elmshorn) an die IT. Entsprechende Kompetenz bzw. Bereitschaft, sich in das Thema einzuarbeiten, muss vorhanden sein.

    Architektur & Standards

    • Zielbild & Referenzarchitektur: Entwicklung von Sicherheits-Zielbildern und Referenzarchitekturen für IAM und die On-Prem-Infrastruktur.

jobs.title: Vice President of Communications and Narrative Strategy
jobs.excerpt: The Proportional Representation HubAmerican democracy is at a breaking point.
jobs.description:
The Proportional Representation Hub

American democracy is at a breaking point. Across the country, voters increasingly find themselves throwing up their hands and turning away from a failing political system. Hyper-partisanship has become entrenched. Fewer than one in ten House races is competitive, and 97% of incumbents cruise to reelection: for most voters, the outcome was settled before a single ballot was cast. Little wonder that politicians feel little pressure to deliver legislative results. Public trust in democratic institutions continues to erode as more and more voters tune out.

But the problem isn’t the politicians. It’s the rules. U.S. elections are distorted by single-winner, winner-take-all districts. A party can win 45% of the vote in districts across a state yet it wins no power. The Supreme Court’s evisceration of the Voting Rights Act has made things much worse: voters in communities of color are being carved up and packed into districts engineered to drown out their voices, and the court has triggered a redistricting death spiral. The need for structural reform has never been more urgent.

There is a fix, and most of the world already uses it: proportional representation. The idea is simple––districts elect several members, and a party that wins a third of the votes wins about a third of the seats. It breaks the two-party monopoly, makes every district competitive, eliminates partisan gerrymandering, and reduces polarization.

The Proportional Representation Hub has launched to help build the next chapter of American democracy. We have raised more than $70 million to lead a campaign to advance proportional representation at the local, state, and federal levels and build a government that delivers again. Proportional representation is the best path to create a democracy that better reflects the diversity of the American people, and the best path to end the redistricting wars.

This work is ambitious: forging unlikely coalitions, winning new legislation and ballot measures, changing public narratives, and developing innovative political strategies. Above all, it demands a cross-partisan movement big enough to persuade the huge majority of Americans who say the political system no longer works for them that our democracy can work far better than it does today.

We are building a team of exceptional leaders working together to reshape the architecture of American democracy itself.

Position Overview

The Vice President of Communications and Narrative Strategy will build and lead the communications, research, and narrative infrastructure necessary to make proportional representation one of the defining democracy reform movements of the 21st century.

The Vice President of Communications and Narrative Strategy will lead all communications, narrative development, public opinion research, digital engagement, media relations, and strategic communications efforts for the Proportional Representation Hub.

This executive will be responsible for shaping how policymakers, voters, journalists, funders, advocates, and opinion leaders understand proportional representation, in the context of other democracy reforms. They will oversee the communications strategies supporting federal, state, and local campaigns while simultaneously building a long-term narrative change effort to help transform the national conversation about democracy and move the idea of proportional representation from the margins to the mainstream.

The Vice President will oversee communications consultants, research firms, polling vendors, creative agencies, digital partners, media strategists, and public affairs consultants. They will also help build communications capacity throughout the broader democracy reform ecosystem, providing strategic guidance and technical support to allied organizations and campaign partners.

The Vice President of Communications and Narrative Strategy will serve as a member of the Senior Leadership Team.

This is a role for a visionary strategist, storyteller, communicator, and movement builder who understands that political change begins with narrative change.

What You’ll Lead

Build a Narrative for Democratic Reform and a Message for Proportional Representation

  • Develop and execute a long-term narrative strategy for multiparty electoral reform and redefine the public conversation about representation, accountability, fairness, and democratic legitimacy.
  • Create messaging frameworks that make proportional representation understandable, compelling, and that resonate across ideological, geographic, racial, and generational divides. Translate complex policy reforms into accessible, motivating narratives that inspire action and support. Ensure campaign communications consistently advance both immediate policy goals and long-term narrative and movement-building objectives.

Lead Narrative Intelligence and Opposition Analysis

  • Build a narrative intelligence operation that continuously tracks public opinion, media narratives, opposition messaging, cultural trends, and emerging political opportunities.
  • Identify threats, attacks, misinformation campaigns, and opposition arguments before they become obstacles to campaign success, and develop proactive communications strategies that inoculate target audiences against predictable attacks and mischaracterizations.
  • Lead ongoing analysis of the political, media, and advocacy landscape to identify opportunities to expand support for proportional representation.
  • Serve as a strategic advisor to the Executive Director and leadership team on reputational risks, emerging opportunities, and changing political conditions.

Drive Winning Campaign Communications

  • Lead communications strategy for federal, state, and local campaigns across the organization’s portfolio.
  • Develop integrated communications plans that leverage earned media, paid media, digital engagement, thought leadership, coalition communications, grassroots storytelling, and public affairs strategies.
  • Ensure campaigns have compelling messaging, rapid response capabilities, media strategies, research support, and public engagement plans.
  • Provide communications strategy, message guidance, narrative support, and technical assistance to allied organizations and coalition partners to support thought leadership across the movement. Create shared tools, research products, messaging resources, narrative frameworks, and strategic guidance that can be deployed by partners nationwide.
  • Build and train a bench of spokespeople and champions for proportional representation, diverse across multiple dimensions including ideologically, and place their voices in traditional and new media channels.
  • Build strong relationships with journalists, editorial boards, influencers, content creators, podcast hosts, and opinion leaders.

Oversee Research and Message Development

  • Lead all public opinion research with polling, focus groups, message testing, audience segmentation, narrative research, and voter insight efforts.
  • Work with leading research firms and strategists to deepen understanding of voter attitudes toward democracy, representation, and political reform.
  • Build systems that allow successful innovations and lessons learned in one campaign to strengthen efforts across the broader movement.

Build a Modern Digital and Media Program

  • Oversee all digital communications, content strategy, social media, paid media, influencer engagement, online organizing, audience growth efforts, and emerging communications platforms.
  • Develop innovative approaches to reach audiences beyond traditional political and advocacy channels.
  • Build a modern communications infrastructure capable of supporting persuasion, movement-building, and rapid-response objectives across federal, state, and local campaigns.

Who you are

You bring a proven track record of leading large-scale communications, public affairs, political, advocacy, or movement-building efforts that have shifted public opinion, shaped public narratives, and contributed to significant policy victories. You have demonstrated experience thinking strategically about the right messengers to the right audiences in the right channels.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 15+ years of senior leadership experience in political communications, public affairs, advocacy, movement-building, media, narrative strategy, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated success leading communications efforts that shifted public opinion, shaped public narratives, influenced policymakers, or contributed to significant policy victories.
  • Deep expertise in message development, polling, audience research, media relations, digital communications, public affairs, and strategic communications planning.
  • Experience overseeing communications for complex, multi-state, national, or international campaigns.
  • Strong understanding of how narrative change contributes to long-term political and social change.
  • Experience managing communications firms, polling vendors, research partners, creative agencies, and large communications budgets.
  • Exceptional writing, storytelling, presentation, and strategic thinking skills.
  • Familiarity with campaign finance regulations (C3/C4 compliance).
  • Strong relationships within national media, digital media, political communications, philanthropy, or advocacy ecosystems.
  • Experience building and managing high-performing teams.
  • A deep commitment to strengthening American democracy and advancing representative government.

Equal Opportunity/Diversity Policy:

Proportional Representation Hub prohibits discrimination of employment, promotion, compensation, terms, conditions, or privileges of employment on the basis of race, color, ancestry, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, sex (including marital and parental status), religion, age, disability, actual or perceived gender identity or expression, weight, personal appearance, family responsibilities, genetic information, economic status, genetic information, veteran’s status, or any other basis prohibited by applicable law. Proportional Representation Hub is an equal opportunity employer and will comply with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination in employment.

A person with fewer years of work experience living in a lower-cost metro area will earn in the bottom third of that range, while a person with more years of experience living in a higher-cost location will earn in the middle third of the range. The highest end of the range reflects the most work experience, the highest-cost metro areas, and more years at the Proportional Representation Hub.

Key Responsibilities

  • Drive new product introduction (NPI) from engineering builds through production release, ensuring OSAT capability meetselectrical/thermal/mechanicalrequirements for FPGA and SoC products.

This is a player-coach role. You'll set the strategy and then execute it alongside a small team in a lean environment. The person who does well here is comfortable working in a cohort retention report and at a sampling activation in the same week.

  • Program strategy and targets: own affiliate revenue as a number you're accountable for, alongside CPA discipline (currently a $25 to $30 band), payback period, and LTV. You'll set the targets and flag early when they need to change.
  • Unit economics: run the channel on contribution margin and LTV:CAC rather than last-click revenue. Understand cohort behaviour well enough to know which creators bring subscribers who retain and which bring subscribers who churn early, and shift spend accordingly.
  • Global go-to-market: lead the program across all three markets, covering creator sourcing, platforms (Roster, Upfluence, AWIN), gifting and PR, and partnerships. Heavy strategic focus on TikTok and TikTok Shop to drive US market entry.
  • Creator roster and lifecycle: build the progression from customer to ambassador to affiliate to top-tier creator. Own onboarding throughput, since time from first contact to first post largely determines how fast the channel can grow. Develop the mid-tail deliberately so revenue isn't concentrated in a handful of relationships.
  • Creative pipeline: treat the content the program generates as a core asset. Build the whitelisting and creator-asset pipeline that feeds paid social, and measure yourself on blended CAC impact alongside the affiliate line.
  • Product seeding and cross-sell: use creators to seed adjacent products, including our Pantry line, as a lower-friction entry point into the core subscription and as an AOV expander for existing subscribers. Build the loop where each product drives demand for the other rather than competing with it.
  • In-real-life events and activations: own the offline side of the program, including sampling, farmers markets, food and wellness festivals, community events, pop-ups, and retail activations. Run creator trips and creator-house programming that produces content at volume. These serve brand, acquisition and content goals together, and you'll be measured across all three.
  • Creator compensation: design and test compensation models, including commission, flat fee, guarantees and tiered leaderboards, that scale profitably. Own rate card discipline and negotiation across a large number of relationships.
  • Attribution and incrementality: own the affiliate stack (Upfluence, AWIN, Roster, Triple Whale) and understand its limits. Run holdouts and geo tests where it matters, and tell leadership when a channel is less incremental than reported.
  • Hands-on leadership: manage and work alongside the affiliate team, coaching through reporting and reliability gaps while carrying your own workload. On a team this size the strategist is also an operator.
