jobs.description:
Splash is partnering with Shortlist Search (Shortlist.net) to recruit this role.

ABOUT SPLASH:

Splash is a global nonprofit organization founded in 2007, headquartered in Seattle, Washington, USA. Since 2007, we have completed more than 2,500 projects that serve over 1.2 million children each day. Currently focused on cities in East and Southern Africa, Splash delivers the clean water, clean toilets, and dignified menstrual health resources that every child deserves through comprehensive water, sanitation, hygiene, and menstrual health (WASH-M) services and behavior change programs across 100% of a city's public schools.

Our vision is global impact without Splash, made possible through partnerships with national governments, co-creation with local communities, and replication far beyond our day-to-day involvement.

In 2019, we began testing and refining Project WISE (WASH in Schools for Everyone), a cost-effective and replicable blueprint designed to reach 100% of public schools in fast-growing, complex cities in partnership with local governments and community leaders. In five years, we achieved our goals in Ethiopia and India, and we began our next phase of expansion in East and Southern Africa in 2025.

Our Core Values: People First | Quality | Honesty | Joy | Learn from Mistakes.

Splash values the unique skills and experiences everyone brings to the organization, and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment. To learn more, please visit splash.org.

POSITION OVERVIEW:

We are seeking a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead our global financial strategy, compliance, risk oversight, and long-term sustainability. Serving on the global management team, the CFO will partner closely with the CEO, Board, and country leaders to build the financial architecture required for government-partnered scale, blended finance, and multi-country expansion.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Financial Strategy, Sustainability, and Blended Finance

  • Lead the development of Splash's long-term financial strategy in alignment with organizational growth, government partnership, and impact goals.
  • Help Splash build a more sophisticated capital strategy that distinguishes between philanthropic funding, catalytic capital, government co-financing, donor-funded infrastructure, technical assistance, and long-term public ownership.
  • Own the financial impact of program changes, tracing how new operational standards or models affect costs, budgets, and donor agreements.
  • Partner with the CEO, Development team, and program leadership to assess how different funding sources can support different needs across the organization.
  • Help answer existential financial questions regarding long-term sustainability, such as how national scale work is sustained beyond initial philanthropy and what happens financially after Splash exits a country.
  • Support financial modeling for government co-financing, donor match requirements, phased implementation, working capital needs, and long-term sustainability.
  • Advise the CEO and Board on tradeoffs related to scale, risk, unrestricted reserves, cost recovery, donor restrictions, and country-level financial exposure.
  • Lead scenario planning and financial modeling for multi-year growth, including delayed disbursements, foreign exchange exposure, government payment timing, implementation shifts, and funding gaps.
  • Build financial models that incorporate inflation, foreign exchange exposure, country-specific cost assumptions, and implementation timing so multi-year budgets are realistic and decision-useful.

Global Financial Management & Reporting

  • Oversee global budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, and financial reporting across Splash's US and international operations.
  • Maintain full ownership of core financial operations, US GAAP compliance, clean audits, and internal controls across all entities.
  • Ensure timely, accurate, and decision-useful reporting for the CEO, management team, Board, Finance Committee, donors, and country teams.
  • Strengthen financial dashboards and analysis so country, regional, and global teams can track burn rates against activities, deliverables, restricted donor budgets, and implementation progress in real time or near-real time.
  • Manage organizational cash flow, reserves, restricted and unrestricted funding, and liquidity planning.
  • Partner with Program and Development teams to ensure budgets, forecasts, and donor reports accurately reflect implementation realities.
  • Support budget modeling for new opportunities, including overall project budgets, donor-specific restricted budgets, match or co-financing assumptions, cost recovery, and implementation timelines.
  • Ensure grant budgets, cost recovery, indirect cost allocation, and donor reporting are disciplined, transparent, and aligned with Splash's operating model.

Government Co-Financing and Public Finance

  • Support the design and financial oversight of government co-financing arrangements, including contribution models, annual workplans, budget alignment, and fund-flow options.
  • Help shape government finance conversations by assessing how public budgets, co-financing deals, and sovereign debt impact our strategic direction and fundraising.
  • Help assess the financial implications of government-funded implementation, direct government procurement, contractor payments, cost-share commitments, and delayed public disbursements.
  • Partner with country teams to ensure government co-financing commitments are financially realistic, well documented, appropriately accounted for, and monitored.
  • Support financial analysis related to public-sector ownership, operations and maintenance, and the long-term transition of responsibility to government systems.
  • Bring practical understanding of the risks and realities of operating in low-income settings, including public finance cycles, procurement constraints, documentation gaps, currency exposure, and varying local accounting capacity.

International Compliance, VAT, Tax, and Risk

  • Ensure compliance with US nonprofit requirements, donor regulations, accounting and audit standards, and relevant international financial regulations.
  • Oversee financial operations across multiple countries and entities, including registration, statutory compliance, local audit requirements, payroll, tax, banking, and accounting practices.
  • Manage VAT, withholding tax, recoverability, exemptions, and other country-level tax issues that affect donor budgets, infrastructure delivery, and local contracting.
  • Lead the annual audit process and manage relationships with external auditors, tax advisors, legal advisors, and other technical consultants.
  • Maintain strong risk management practices across global financial operations, including internal controls, segregation of duties, fraud prevention, procurement controls, and documentation standards.

Systems, Controls, and Operational Discipline

  • Build and maintain strong financial systems, policies, processes, and internal controls that support a growing global organization.
  • Strengthen financial technology, reporting tools, data integrity, and cross-country accounting processes.
  • Build and enforce the accounting and reporting architecture needed to track restricted funds by donor, project, activity, deliverable, country, budget line, and spending status.
  • Strengthen budgeting, forecasting, financial controls, cost documentation, and approval processes so they are clear, efficient, and scalable.
  • Ensure finance processes support procurement, contracting, and implementation without making finance a bottleneck.
  • Drive a culture of financial accountability, transparency, and timely decision-making.

Team Leadership and Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Lead, mentor, and strengthen Splash's global finance team.
  • Build financial capacity across country teams and non-finance leaders so budget ownership is distributed and disciplined.
  • Partner closely with Program, Development, Operations, and country leadership to align financial resources with program delivery and organizational priorities.
  • Translate complex financial issues into clear, practical guidance for colleagues who are not finance specialists.
  • Serve as a trusted partner to the CEO, Treasurer, Finance Committee, and Board.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Typically 15+ years of progressively senior financial leadership.
  • Deep expertise in US nonprofit finance, including US 501(c)(3) operations, US GAAP, IRS reporting, audit requirements, and board governance.
  • Significant global finance leadership experience in an international nonprofit, NGO, foundation, development finance institution, or other mission-driven organization operating across multiple countries.
  • Strong knowledge of international financial management, including IFRS (and IPSAS where relevant), donor compliance, grants management, restricted funding, audits, internal controls, statutory compliance, procurement, VAT/tax, multi-currency operations, and financial risk management.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead financial strategy, planning, forecasting, financial modeling, and multi-year, multi-country budgeting in complex operating environments.
  • Hands-on experience working in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, or Southeast Asia, is preferred.
  • Experience supporting government co-financing, public-private partnerships, infrastructure financing, development finance, or blended finance is strongly preferred.
  • Proven ability to work effectively with Boards, Finance Committees, CEOs, and senior leadership teams.
  • Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Public Administration, or a related field preferred. CPA, MBA, or equivalent professional qualification strongly valued.
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel, financial reporting systems, accounting platforms, grant management tools, and financial reporting and analytics.

jobs.description:
Telehealth Nurse Practitioner

Join a remote, member-facing clinical team helping patients safely navigate the first critical days after discharge. In this full-time telehealth role, you’ll conduct Transitional Care Management visits within 14 days of discharge, complete comprehensive clinical assessments, reconcile medications, identify red flags, and coordinate care that helps reduce avoidable readmissions. This is a strong fit for a licensed Nurse Practitioner who is comfortable working independently on video, documenting same-day, and supporting members across multiple states.

Opportunity

This is a full-time, exempt Telehealth Transitional Care Nurse Practitioner role focused on post-discharge care. You’ll work remotely with members and caregivers through virtual visits, helping close care gaps, support safe recovery, and escalate urgent clinical concerns when needed.

Role details:

  • Employment type: Full-time, exempt
  • Work model: Remote / telehealth
  • Schedule: Core hours of 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM Central Time, Monday through Friday
  • Weekend coverage: Rotating weekend coverage required for urgent or emergent needs, which may include a Saturday visit when clinically necessary
  • Start: ASAP
  • Compensation: $135,000 salary

What You Will Own

Transitional Care Management Visits

  • Conduct telehealth TCM visits within the required post-discharge window.
  • Perform comprehensive clinical assessments for recently discharged members.
  • Complete medication reconciliation and identify potential safety, adherence, or care-continuity concerns.
  • Support members and caregivers through video visit connection steps, basic troubleshooting, and maintaining a private, HIPAA-compliant encounter environment.

Clinical Escalation and Care Coordination

  • Identify acute clinical needs and escalate urgent findings according to clinical protocols.
  • Serve as a first-line clinical escalation resource for care coordinators and support staff regarding member status, red-flag symptoms, or scheduling issues with clinical implications.
  • Coordinate with care team members who interface with PCPs, specialists, and discharge planning teams to help close care gaps and reduce readmission risk.
  • Adjust daily visit sequencing as needed based on member cancellations, discharge timing, and care priorities.

Documentation, Quality, and Compliance

  • Document all encounters completely and accurately.
  • Submit charts no later than the date of service to support timely coding, quality reporting, and claims submission.
  • Maintain compliance with HIPAA, state licensure, and payer-specific documentation requirements.
  • Participate in ongoing clinical training, chart audit feedback sessions, and quality improvement initiatives.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • Active, unrestricted Nurse Practitioner licensure in at least three of the following states: OH, CA, NY, IN, KY, PA, LA, MI, TN, MO.
  • Active national board certification through AANP or ANCC as an FNP, AGNP, or equivalent adult/geriatric-focused certification.
  • Minimum of 2 years of clinical experience.
  • Comfort delivering care through video visits and communicating clearly with members and caregivers in a remote setting.
  • Ability to work a dependable weekday schedule with rotating weekend coverage for urgent or emergent clinical needs.
  • Strong comfort using EMR documentation platforms, video-visit software, and desktop or mobile point-of-care technology.
  • Ability to complete accurate same-day documentation for all encounters.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Prior telemedicine or telehealth experience.
  • Transitional Care Management or post-discharge care experience.
  • Experience working with Medicare Advantage populations.
  • Familiarity with HEDIS, STAR measures, and value-based care documentation standards.
  • Experience in a fast-paced, discharge-driven scheduling environment.

Remote Work and Technology Requirements

  • Dedicated, private, HIPAA-compliant workspace free from background noise and visual distractions during scheduled video visits.
  • Reliable high-speed internet connection sufficient for stable, uninterrupted video visits.
  • Personal computer and webcam setup that can support secure video visits and required clinical documentation tools.
  • Ability to remain seated, attentive, and engaged on camera for consecutive video visits throughout the scheduled shift.

Equal Opportunity

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. This job description reflects the general nature of the role and is not an exhaustive list of duties.

Compensation

The expected total compensation range is USD 135,000 Yearly.

Apply now and get a response within 24 hours.

Salary: $135,000 / year

jobs.description:
About the Job

Reporting to the CISO, the Security Architect will ensure that stakeholder security requirements necessary to protect the organization’s mission and business processes are adequately addressed in all aspects of enterprise architecture — including reference models, segment and solution architectures, and the resulting systems supporting those missions and business processes. This role carries responsibility for both blockchain and non-blockchain security, and should have experience with both. This position has high visibility and direct responsibility for the effective and efficient architecture of the Security Systems in addition to company and product systems. The role also drives process refinement and implementation, cross-team/discipline collaboration, and maintenance of internal and external stakeholder relationships.

Responsibilities

As part of our team, your core responsibilities will be:

• Implement strategy defined by the CISO, with some input on the same

• Have agency to visit, introspect and influence technology functions to champion maturity of security-critical processes

• Review supplier and partner security profiles and submissions

• Manage existing relationships and tooling to ensure licenses and entitlements are fully utilized

• Map security initiatives and benchmarks to established risk and maturity models

• Do what’s right, so that current and future compliance initiatives come naturally

• Have a finger on the pulse of the industry, proactively maintain knowledge of emerging

tactics, tools, and solutions, and advise zerohash stakeholders as appropriate

• Engage with community and sector-specific organisations and working groups

• Champion defence in depth, layering protective controls and segmenting systems as appropriate

• Architect, design, and implement security solutions, tools, and services to protect zerohash’s cloud network environment in collaboration with zerohash engineering teams

• Develop and maintain requirements and standards for capabilities that support security operations, threat detection, intelligence, and incident response functions

• Conduct regular system tests and ensure continuous monitoring of network security

• Establish disaster recovery procedures and conduct breach of security drills

• Promptly respond to all security incidents and provide thorough post-event analyses

• Work with product management and software engineering teams during all phases of the SDLC to ensure that applications are designed and implemented securely

• Leverage threat models to define requirements and identify gaps to address threats

• Perform security reviews of infrastructure, products, and services

• Test web3 and web2 applications and underlying systems for vulnerabilities using both tools and manual techniques; manage the remediation of findings through resolution

• Help develop secure coding standards and training materials based on findings seen in the zerohash environment, to empower engineers to write more secure code

• Research vulnerabilities specific to blockchain technologies and incorporate this knowledge into zerohash’s security practices

• Provide technical expertise on trends and emerging standards in the cloud security and blockchain landscape

• Work closely with team members to enhance, implement, and configure scalable security technologies, and improve detection and response capabilities

• Implement, review, and maintain strong access controls and identity roles within the cloud infrastructure

• Support tooling evaluations and rollouts across the Security program (e.g., SIEM platform evaluation) in partnership with the broader Security team

• Support our CISO and Security team on additional security projects, as needed

Requirements

Baseline skills/experiences/attributes:

• Minimum 10+ years of experience designing and implementing security infrastructure services in AWS, and other security solutions including IAM, EDR, MDM, SIEM, KMS, and PAM

• Minimum 5+ years of experience in blockchain security

• Experience in AppSec including SAST, DAST, open vulnerability management, and pen testing

jobs.excerpt: The RoleWe're looking for a commercially minded Growth Strategist to help shape and deliver growth strategies for an exciting portfolio of consumer brands.
jobs.description:
The Role

We're looking for a commercially minded Growth Strategist to help shape and deliver growth strategies for an exciting portfolio of consumer brands.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys getting under the skin of a business—understanding how customers are acquired, where they convert, what keeps them coming back and, ultimately, where the biggest opportunities for growth lie.

You'll initially work closely with our Head of Growth, supporting the strategy and performance of a portfolio of clients. As you establish yourself in the role, you'll take increasing ownership of client reporting, strategic recommendations and quarterly business reviews.

You'll also work alongside a Growth Executive as part of an eight-person Growth team, combining strategic thinking with hands-on analysis to help ambitious brands grow.

Our Client

A leading Shopify agency specialising in the intersection ofdesign, technology and growth.

They partner with ambitious consumer brands to build and grow exceptional DTC businesses. The team of around 25 specialists spans design, development, growth and client services, giving them the ability to support brands far beyond simply building a great website.

AShopify Premier Partner,Recharge Premier Partner,Klaviyo Gold Partner,Skio Partnerand a certifiedB Corp.

Their clients range from exciting brands in the early stages of their journey through to established businesses generating significant subscription revenue. Across the Growth team, they work on the full customer journey—from acquisition and conversion through to retention and lifetime value.

As their client portfolio continues to grow, they are looking for a talented Growth Strategist to join them.

What You'll Be Doing
Developing growth strategies

You'll analyse each client's business and customer journey to identify the biggest opportunities for growth.

This will include:

  • Mapping the customer journey from acquisition through to repeat purchase.

  • Identifying opportunities to improve conversion, AOV, CAC and customer lifetime value.

  • Understanding where brands are underperforming against their potential.

  • Turning data and insight into clear, commercially focused recommendations.

  • Helping clients prioritise the initiatives most likely to have a meaningful impact.

Looking at the bigger picture

This isn't a role focused on a single marketing channel.

You'll take a holistic view of growth, understanding how areas including paid media, retention, email, subscription and eCommerce performance work together.

Using data to tell the story

You'll be comfortable getting into the numbers and translating performance data into meaningful commercial insight.

Rather than simply reporting on what has happened, you'll help clients understandwhy it happened—and what they should do next.

Over time, you'll take ownership of client reporting and quarterly business reviews, becoming a trusted strategic partner to the brands you work with.

Working collaboratively

You'll work closely with specialists across the business, including teams in paid media, retention, design, development and client services.

Your role will be to connect the dots, ensuring activity across different channels is aligned with the wider growth strategy and focused on the commercial outcomes that matter most.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone with a strong understanding of how modern DTC and eCommerce businesses grow.

You may currently be working in a growth, eCommerce, strategy or performance-focused role, either agency-side or in-house. Most importantly, you'll be commercially curious and enjoy using data to solve problems.

You'll ideally bring:

  • Around five years' experience in a growth, eCommerce or digital strategy-focused role.

  • A strong understanding of DTC and eCommerce business models.

  • Experience analysing customer journeys and identifying growth opportunities.

  • A good understanding of key commercial metrics, including CAC, LTV, AOV and conversion rate.

  • The ability to turn complex data into clear and actionable recommendations.

  • Experience working across multiple areas of digital growth, such as acquisition, retention, email and subscription.

  • Strong communication and presentation skills.

  • The confidence to work directly with clients and build trusted relationships.

Why Join?

This is a fantastic opportunity to work with a diverse portfolio of ambitious consumer brands while developing your career within a growing and highly specialist agency.

You'll work closely with experienced growth leaders, gain exposure to a wide range of business challenges and have the opportunity to take increasing ownership of client strategy as you grow in the role.

If you're someone who loves understanding what makes businesses grow—and wants to work across acquisition, conversion, retention and the wider customer journey—this could be the perfect next step.

Our client is proud to be an equal opportunities employer and is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Clarity RCM is a rapidly growing revenue cycle management company on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing companies. We manage billing, credentialing, and account management for private dermatology practices nationwide, and we are expanding those operations into orthopedics. We are building the team that grows with us.

This role is for a certified coder who brings versatility. You will primarily support our core dermatology accounts while using your orthopedic knowledge to support our expanding musculoskeletal line of business. You will not be plugging in codes in a silo. You will own coding integrity for a defined set of clients and support account managers across specialties, touching client compliance, denial resolution, and payer navigation along the way.

The people who thrive here are the ones who find the documentation gaps before they cause denials, ask sharp questions, and figure things out.

Growth is real here. It is also earned, not given.

This role is for USA candidates only

What You'll Do

  • Code across specialties. Translate clinical documentation into accurate ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS Level II codes, weighted heavily toward dermatology (biopsies, destructions, Mohs, excisions), with the ability to code orthopedic visits and procedures as needed. Apply specialty-specific and global surgery modifiers (25, 59, XE, XS, XP, XU) within NCCI edits so claims go out clean.
  • Own documentation quality. Validate provider notes against current E/M leveling guidelines on both office visits and procedure-heavy encounters, and go directly to practice managers and physicians when something is incomplete or ambiguous. They are not coding experts. You are.
  • Resolve denials. Research and work complex coding-related denials across major payers. Understand why a claim was denied and execute the right path forward, using approved AI tools to draft stronger appeals and move faster.
  • Work in client systems. Navigate ModMed (EMA), EZDERM, Nextech, eCW, and other modern EHR and practice management platforms fluently.
  • Make the operation better. Flag recurring documentation errors and payer trends that delay revenue, recommend fixes, and pick up new specialties and workflows as we grow. There is no formal curriculum here. The exposure is built into the work.

Who You Are

  • Certified and versatile. Active AAPC credential, 1 to 2 years of medical coding experience, strong dermatology expertise. Orthopedic coding experience is a major plus.
  • A self-starter who handles ambiguity. This is a fast-growing company and not everything is defined. You do not wait for perfect instructions before digging into a complex report or picking up a new specialty workflow.
  • AI-native. You already use AI tools in your work, or you are actively curious about how they can make you better. You think about efficiency, not just effort.
  • Clear and steady under pressure. Practice managers and providers can be demanding. You stay calm, give straight compliance-backed answers, and follow through.
  • Here to contribute, not to be developed. We will give you exposure across multiple specialties in a scaling business. What you do with it is on you.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary
  • 90% employer-covered health, dental, and vision
  • Remote, full-time position
  • Real exposure to every element of a scaling RCM operation
  • A team that moves fast and rewards people who do the same

About Drips

Drips helps organizations build stronger customer and member relationships through personalized, two-way conversations at scale. We combine AI-powered engagement with strategy, design, and managed execution to help people take meaningful next steps across the customer journey.

Our Corporate IT team keeps the technology, identity, and security foundation that Drips runs on scaling safely alongside a fast-growing business — from the tools our people use every day to the governance and automation that keep IT out of the way.

About the role

We're hiring a Sr. Manager, Corporate IT to lead and grow our Corporate IT function as Drips scales. This is a hands-on leadership role: you'll manage a team of IT professionals, lead corporate IT operations and internal technology services across identity, endpoints, corporate SaaS, ITSM, device lifecycle, vendors, documentation, and operational automation, and act as the connective tissue between IT, InfoSec, and the rest of the company.

You'll report to the CIO / CISO and partner closely with InfoSec and Corporate Systems to make sure that as we grow, our security posture, compliance obligations, and IT governance scale right alongside the business rather than becoming an afterthought or a bottleneck.

The right person is equally comfortable in a strategy conversation with a department leader and in the weeds of an identity, endpoint, or access issue. You'll mature our IT governance and control environment, own vendor relationships, and lead our push on ticket deflection and AI-powered automation so the team's time goes toward higher-value work instead of repetitive tickets.

Success in this role means IT is a well-run, well-managed function that scales with the business, is trusted by leaders across the company, and is measurably reducing manual and repetitive support work through automation.

Department: IT
Reports to: CIO / CISO
Direct reports: IT Associate, Sr IT Associate
Location: Remote
Travel: Limited travel required, estimated at 1 to 2 weeks per year

What you'll do

Lead and grow the team

  • Lead, manage, and grow a team of IT professionals: hire, coach, set priorities, and own performance and development.
  • Champion a culture of exceptional customer service across the IT team, ensuring every employee interaction — from a help desk ticket to an executive request — is handled with responsiveness, professionalism, and ownership.

Run and mature core IT operations

  • Administration for our core stack, including Microsoft 365, Entra ID and related identity/IAM tooling, endpoint management (MDM) and EDR, and our ITSM/ticketing platform.
  • Build and mature IT governance: access controls, change management, provisioning/de-provisioning, and documentation that scale with the business instead of relying on individual heroics.
  • Manage identity lifecycle, account provisioning/deprovisioning, and role-based access governance across business systems driven by control requirements and risk decisions defined by InfoSec.
  • Lead device lifecycle strategy (procurement, imaging, deployment, recovery, retirement) and endpoint security posture.
  • Build IT capacity planning, documentation, and continuity practices so the function isn't dependent on any single person, including yourself.

Partner across the business

  • Support InfoSec on our security and compliance program (including ISO 27001, HITRUST, and related frameworks), and support client security questionnaires and audits as needed.
  • Serve as a trusted partner to department and business leaders, translating their goals and project needs into IT priorities and helping their initiatives succeed.
  • Vendor management, software licensing, renewals, and Corporate IT budget/spend across the corporate IT stack.
  • Represent IT in cross-functional planning for new tools, integrations, and company initiatives as Drips scales, including consolidating redundant or fragmented tooling and establishing a formal intake and evaluation process for new technology requests.

Drive automation and measurable outcomes

  • Own and drive ticket deflection and AI automation: expand self-service, AI-assisted support (including our internal AI help desk agent), and workflow automation to reduce ticket volume and speed up resolution, and use those gains to hold the team's size steady while supporting a growing employee base as Drips scales.
  • Report on IT operations (ticket volume, SLAs, automation adoption, project delivery) to leadership on a regular cadence.
  • Own a regular Corporate IT operating cadence, including a weekly IT operations review, recurring IT/InfoSec coordination meetings, a monthly governance review, and quarterly business reviews with stakeholders.

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years of progressive IT experience, including 3+ years directly managing and developing an IT team — hiring, coaching, delegating, and owning performance — not just individual-contributor experience.
  • Hands-on depth across our core stack: Microsoft 365, Entra ID and identity/access management, endpoint (MDM) and EDR tooling for a mixed fleet of Windows and iOS devices, and an ITSM/ticketing platform, ideally owned or heavily operated at scale.
  • Direct experience building or maturing IT governance, security, and compliance programs inside a regulated or high-growth SaaS environment, with familiarity with frameworks such as ISO 27001, HITRUST, SOC 2, and HIPAA-adjacent requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience driving ticket deflection and AI-assisted IT automation (self-service, AI agents, workflow automation) with measurable results.
  • Strong cross-functional partnership skills — able to sit with department leaders and executives and translate their goals into IT priorities.
  • Experience working with and supporting GenAI tools like Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc. within the corporate technology environment.
  • Experience managing vendors, software licensing, and an IT budget.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, comfortable moving between technical detail and executive-level conversation.
  • Sound judgment operating in an environment where priorities and risk shift quickly.

Strongly preferred

  • Experience in an established, mature corporate technology environment, with recent experience in a PE-backed, SaaS, mid-market, high-growth company.
  • Experience in healthcare, insurance, financial services, or another highly regulated industry.
  • Experience supporting enterprise client security questionnaires, audits, or vendor risk reviews.

We are looking for a Cloud Partner Channel Sales Manager to build our cloud reseller channel from the ground up. Your mandate is to design, launch, and scale a partner program that enables cloud resellers, MSPs, and marketplace channel partners to resell VyOS subscriptions through the private offer mechanisms of the three major clouds.

What Success Looks Like

  • Revenue growth generated through cloud partners and resellers.
  • A repeatable, documented program that scales without proportional headcount.

Skills and experience

  • 5+ years in channel sales, partner management, or cloud marketplace roles, with direct experience selling or transacting through AWS, Azure, and GCP marketplaces.
  • Hands-on experience with private offers on at least two of the three major clouds, including channel/multiparty private offer mechanics (CPPO, MPO, or GCP channel offers).
  • A track record of building or significantly scaling a partner or channel program, ideally at an ISV or software vendor.
  • Strong customer and partner management skills: you have owned relationships through the full lifecycle, from recruitment to renewal.
  • Commercial fluency in subscription software: pricing, margins, discounting, multi-year terms, and marketplace billing models.
  • Ability to operate autonomously in a remote, globally distributed team, managing partners across time zones.

Would be a plus:

  • Existing relationships with cloud resellers, distributors, or hyperscaler marketplace teams.
  • Experience with hyperscaler co-sell programs (AWS ISV Accelerate, Microsoft co-sell, Google Cloud Partner Advantage).
  • Additional languages

What We Offer

  • A greenfield mandate with direct CRO sponsorship and visibility across the company.
  • Remote-first work with flexible hours.
  • Competitive compensation with a variable component tied to program growth.
  • The opportunity to shape how an established open source networking vendor goes to market in the cloud.

Our Mission

Powering a connected world, engineering for the future.

We believe that the future of networking lies in open collaboration, continuous innovation, and delivering solutions that keep the world connected, efficiently and securely.

Our Core Values

Our values define who we are as a team and how we approach our work every day:

  • Respect: We believe in fostering a respectful environment where we value each other's perspectives and contributions. We maintain a deep respect for our colleagues, our open-source community, and our clients, ensuring that all interactions are guided by understanding, professionalism, and empathy.

jobs.excerpt: This is an internal role at Weekday.  Not a role by a client.
jobs.description:
This is an internal role at Weekday. Not a role by a client.

  • Role type: Full time
  • Location: Remote
  • Working with: CEO and Cofounder

Weekday is an AI-native recruiting platform. We are backed by Y Combinator and Venture Highway (now General Catalyst). We have built the largest white collar talent database in India and have built tools to run outbound recruiting campaigns to them.

About the role

You’ll work closely with the founders on some of the most important problems at the company.

There isn’t a fixed lane for this role. What you work on will depend on what the company needs at the time. That could mean figuring out why a product isn’t growing, launching a new product or market, improving an internal process, working with customers, researching a new opportunity, or taking on a project that simply doesn’t have an obvious owner yet.

This is a hands-on role. We’re not looking for someone whose job ends at analysing a problem and making a recommendation. You should be comfortable getting into the details and doing the work yourself.

As the company grows, the problems you work on will change. We expect the role to change with them.

What you’ll work on

Depending on the week, you might:

  • Take a new idea from a rough hypothesis to something we can actually test
  • Dig into a part of the business that isn’t working well, understand why, and fix it
  • Work on growth for an existing product, including talking to customers, improving positioning, running experiments, or helping close important deals
  • Research a new market, product, partnership, or business opportunity and decide whether it is worth pursuing
  • Build a process or internal tool where none exists today
  • Work with product and engineering to turn customer or business problems into product changes
  • Take ownership of projects that cut across teams and would otherwise fall between the cracks
  • Help the founders make decisions by getting to the underlying facts quickly

Some projects will last a few days. Others may become something you own for months.

What we’re looking for

  • You’re good at figuring things out. You can take a vaguely defined problem, ask the right questions, and get to a useful answer without needing a detailed brief.
  • You’re comfortable doing the work yourself. If something requires talking to customers, going through data, writing copy, building a spreadsheet, or putting together a quick script, you’ll do it.
  • You have good business judgement. You can distinguish between something that is interesting and something that actually matters.
  • You’re comfortable with numbers and technology. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you should be able to work with data and use technology to make yourself more effective.
  • You communicate clearly. You can write well, explain what you’ve learned, and say when something isn’t working.
  • You take ownership. Once you take something on, the founders shouldn’t have to keep checking whether it is moving.
  • You care about details. A lot of this job involves noticing things other people miss and following through on them.
  • You’re comfortable with ambiguity. Priorities will change and you won’t always have a playbook to follow.

We care less about whether you’ve had a “Founder’s Office” title before. You could come from startups, consulting, product, growth, operations, investing, or something else entirely. What matters is whether you can learn quickly and get useful things done.

What you get

You’ll work directly with the founders and get exposure to most parts of the company.

You’ll see how decisions get made, work on problems before they have dedicated teams around them, and have a lot of room to take ownership. If something you start becomes important enough, there’s a good chance you’ll continue to own it.

This role is a good fit for someone who eventually wants to build a company, run a business or product line, or become a generalist operator at an early-stage company.

Context for This Role

We are building Coherence OS because we believe the next era of technology requires more than speed and scale — it requires meaning, integrity, and systems that hold over time.

This translation work is part of a broader effort to make advanced systems accessible across languages — not as content, but as infrastructure.

This is not a typical translation project.

You are not translating marketing copy or generic product documentation. You are helping extend access to a system designed to support individuals in navigating and participating in a rapidly changing economic landscape shaped by AI.

The work requires precision, judgment, and respect for meaning. Much of what you will translate involves concepts that must remain structurally intact across languages — not just linguistically accurate, but conceptually faithful.

We are looking for translators who understand that language is not just communication — it is access.

About Coherence OS

Coherence OS is an AI-native operating system focused on preserving human meaning, identity, and ethical coherence in the age of advanced automation.

We are building foundational infrastructure intended to support long-lived, global-scale systems — not short-term SaaS experiments.

This role is for someone who wants to contribute to systems that will matter over time.

Company Stage & Visibility

Coherence OS is in its earliest build phase. We are intentionally operating with a minimal public footprint while core systems, filings, and internal foundations are being finalized.

We have a minimal public website. Full context about the company, mission, and roadmap will be shared during the interview process.

Scope of Work

  • Translate structured system content from English into Vietnamese
  • Preserve meaning, tone, and conceptual integrity — not just literal phrasing
  • Maintain consistency across terminology and frameworks
  • Flag ambiguities or areas requiring clarification
  • Collaborate asynchronously with our internal team when needed

Requirements

  • Native or near-native fluency in Vietnamese
  • Strong proficiency in English (written comprehension required)
  • Ability to translate abstract and conceptual material accurately
  • High attention to detail and consistency
  • Comfortable working independently with minimal oversight

Compensation Options

You may choose between two options:

Option 1: Cash Payment (Project-Based)

  • Fixed, one-time payment upon completion of the translation
  • No ongoing access or involvement beyond the project

Option 2: Platform Access (Preferred Option)

  • 2 years of full platform access (retail value: $4,800+ USD)
  • Access to systems designed to build, operate, and support income-generating activities
  • Removes the need to pay separately for tools, automation, and execution support typically required to run these activities

This option is intended for individuals who think beyond a single project and want access to infrastructure they can continue using over time.

While the retail cost is $4,800+, the actual value is not capped at that number — it depends on how the system is used. Many individuals will spend significantly more than this over time trying to assemble comparable capabilities independently.

Most candidates who recognize the long-term value of access over one-time payment choose Option 2.

Selection Priority

Due to the nature of this work and the role it plays in expanding access globally, priority will be given to candidates who select Platform Access

How to Apply

Please submit:

  • Your CV (in English)
  • A brief note confirming your language pair and availability
  • Which compensation option you prefer

Applications must be submitted in English. Submissions in other languages will not be reviewed.

Closing

This role is best suited for individuals who want to contribute to something being built with long-term intent.

If you are looking for a standard translation task, this will likely feel different.

If you are interested in contributing to systems designed to operate at scale, across languages, and over time — you will likely find this work meaningful.

jobs.description:
Senior Payments Operations Lead

Location: Remote
Employment: Full-time
Level: Senior individual contributor
Preferred geography: Ukraine or Eastern Europe

About the role

MCR Group builds and scales subscription-based digital products across international markets. Since launch, the company has grown 20x, and we are now building the payments infrastructure needed for our next stage of growth.

We are looking for a Senior Payments Operations Lead to own and develop our payment operations function. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role for someone who combines deep subscription-payments expertise with strong analytical, commercial, and operational skills.

You will have two core missions:

  1. Build our multi-PSP infrastructure: identify, negotiate with, onboard, and connect the right Payment Service Providers.
  2. Own ongoing payment performance: analyze transactions, identify problems and opportunities, and improve approval rates, renewal performance, and revenue recovery.

This is a greenfield opportunity. You will not inherit a mature payments organization or a fixed operating model. You will have the freedom and responsibility to build the function using your experience, judgment, and vision.

What you will own

Payment infrastructure and PSP strategy

  • Assess the current payment setup and define the future multi-PSP strategy.
  • Identify and evaluate new PSPs, acquirers, and payment partners.
  • Lead commercial negotiations, onboarding, contracting, and escalation processes.
  • Build a resilient multi-provider setup that reduces concentration and operational risk.
  • Design and implement payment orchestration, routing, cascading, and failover logic.
  • Work with legal, finance, product, and engineering teams throughout PSP integrations.
  • Establish a structured approach to PSP performance reviews and relationship management.

The initial infrastructure-building phase is expected to be especially intensive during the first six months. Once the core setup is established, the focus will shift toward continuous optimization and maintenance.

Payment performance and daily operations

  • Monitor payment performance across all PSPs, products, countries, and transaction types.
  • Analyze authorization rates, decline rates, decline reasons, renewal sequences, and payment failures.
  • Identify performance issues and revenue opportunities through daily analysis.
  • Define retry, cascading, routing, and dunning strategies.
  • Improve failed-payment recovery and reduce involuntary churn.
  • Build or request the reports needed to make informed operational decisions.
  • Create dashboards, alerts, and monitoring processes that identify payment issues before they materially affect revenue.
  • Investigate changes in performance and coordinate corrective actions with internal teams and external providers.

As additional PSPs are connected, the analytical and operational complexity of the role will grow. Strong attention to detail and comfort working with numbers every day are essential.

Risk, disputes, and process ownership

  • Build and manage the operational framework for disputes, refunds, chargebacks, and fraud monitoring.
  • Analyze related reports, trends, ratios, and root causes.
  • Define responsibilities, workflows, escalation paths, and internal controls.
  • Maintain compliance with PSP risk programs and relevant card-scheme requirements.
  • Partner with the team member responsible for processing individual refunds and chargebacks.

You will not be expected to handle every individual refund or dispute personally. Your responsibility will be to understand these processes deeply, build the right structure, monitor results, and ensure the function operates effectively.

What we are looking for

Essential experience

  • At least five years of relevant experience in payment operations, payment performance, acquiring, or subscription billing.
  • Direct experience working with multiple PSPs, such as Stripe, Adyen, Braintree, Checkout.com, or comparable providers.
  • Proven experience evaluating and onboarding PSPs and managing multi-provider payment setups.
  • Experience building or operating payment orchestration, routing, and cascading systems.
  • Strong experience with recurring subscriptions, renewals, retries, dunning, and involuntary-churn reduction.
  • Experience managing more than $12 million in payment volume.
  • Strong knowledge of payment metrics, including authorization rates, decline reasons, recovery rates, dispute ratios, and fraud ratios.
  • Deep understanding of refunds, disputes, chargebacks, fraud monitoring, and card-scheme requirements.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate payment data into clear priorities and actions.
  • Experience building reporting, dashboards, and operational monitoring from the ground up.
  • Confidence working directly with senior executives, technical teams, legal partners, and external payment providers.
  • Strong English communication and negotiation skills.

Particularly relevant backgrounds

We are especially interested in candidates from high-volume, international subscription businesses, consumer applications, digital products, SaaS, streaming, or comparable recurring-revenue environments.

Experience limited to one-time payments or sectors with fundamentally different PSP-rotation models may be less relevant unless accompanied by substantial subscription-payment expertise.

What success looks like

During your first six months, you will be expected to:

  • Build a clear understanding of our payment flows, performance, risks, and reporting gaps.
  • Define the target PSP and payment-orchestration strategy.
  • Establish reliable payment-performance reporting and operational alerts.
  • Lead the evaluation, negotiation, and onboarding of additional PSPs.
  • Create structured processes for payment incidents, disputes, fraud, and PSP escalations.
  • Identify and begin implementing opportunities to improve authorization and renewal performance.

Over time, success will be measured through:

  • Stronger approval and renewal rates.

Full-Time · Remote (Canada) · Eterio Realities Inc. / Fabstation

[Salary range: $ 160,000 - 200,000 CAD

About the Role

Fabstation puts AR work instructions directly onto structural steel during fabrication. Our software runs on AR tablets and headsets on real shop floors across North America, overlaying CAD-driven guidance onto multi-tonne steel assemblies during fit-up, welding, and inspection. We are cash-flow positive, growing fast, and used daily in production.

We are hiring a Senior Computer Vision Engineer to own our real-time 3D object tracking capability: locking a CAD model onto a physical steel member and keeping it locked as the user moves around it. Tracking is core to our product, and we build it in-house.

You will build on internal groundwork already underway and own the road from there: architecture, implementation, optimization, and production hardening. This is a role for someone who wants to own a hard, central problem end-to-end and see it shipped into the hands of real tradespeople, not maintain someone else's pipeline.

What You'll Do

  • Own the on-device object tracking core end-to-end, from architecture through production
  • Design and implement real-time, model-based 6DoF pose estimation and continuous tracking for textureless steel structures, using CAD models as the tracking reference
  • Fuse object tracking with platform world tracking (visual-inertial odometry), depth, and IMU data; own tracking-loss detection, drift management, and recovery
  • Optimize native C++ vision pipelines for iOS and Apple silicon: rendering, CPU/GPU budgets, and sustained frame rates on iPad or headset hardware
  • Extend tracking to large structures: partial visibility, multi-region strategies, and CAD mesh preprocessing from IFC/STEP - type exports
  • Integrate native modules with Unity via a plugin bridge, and work with our Unity team from prototype through release
  • Define tracking quality metrics and benchmark against real shop-floor conditions: occlusion, mixed lighting, and cluttered scenes of visually similar material

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of professional experience in computer vision or a closely related field, with a focus on real-time systems
  • Shipped at least one real-time computer vision feature on a mobile platform (iOS or Android)
  • Strong modern C++; Python is an asset
  • Solid foundation in 3D geometry: camera models, calibration, projective geometry, and linear algebra
  • Working command of nonlinear least-squares optimization (Gauss–Newton / Levenberg–Marquardt) and pose parameterization on SE(3)
  • Hands-on experience with pose estimation and object tracking algorithms
  • Experience integrating native C++ libraries with Unity, or equivalent native-mobile plugin experience
  • Strong profiling and optimization skills on ARM (frame budgets, Instruments or equivalent)
  • Working proficiency with OpenCV

Preferred Qualifications

  • Model-based 3D object tracking (region-based, edge-based, or hybrid approaches)
  • Metal and GPU compute on Apple silicon
  • Visual-inertial odometry or SLAM; ARKit (ARCore an asset)
  • State estimation and multi-sensor fusion: Kalman filtering, factor graphs (Ceres, g2o, GTSAM), extrinsic calibration, and time synchronization
  • On-device ML deployment: Core ML, ONNX Runtime, or Unity Sentis; learning-based pose estimation or refinement that has shipped on-device
  • CAD data handling: mesh processing and decimation, IFC/STEP-style exports
  • Background in industrial vision, robotics, or augmented reality

How to Apply

We prioritize applications that demonstrate hands-on, real-time computer vision work. Please include:

  • A brief introduction and a summary of relevant experience
  • Links to your GitHub profile, portfolio, or publications
  • One or two examples of real-time pose estimation, tracking, or 3D vision work you built, links or short write-ups

Working at Eterio

Eterio Realities Inc. (Victoria, BC) is the company behind Fabstation, an AR-enabled manufacturing execution system for structural steel fabrication. We are a small senior team; you will have direct ownership, direct access to real customer shop floors, and a short path from your code to a tradesperson's hands.

Eterio Realities is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada.

Salary: $160,000 – $200,000 / year

As a QA Engineer, you'll own test planning, functional and exploratory testing, and user acceptance testing (UAT) across zerohash's product stack. This is an opportunity to shape testing practices and quality standards as the team scales, with visibility into every product area and a direct line to release quality.

Responsibilities

  • Test coverage: Design, document, and execute functional and exploratory test cases for API- and SDK-based product flows.
  • Automation testing: Pick up automation work on an ad hoc or on-demand basis, addressing automation tech debt and critical-flow gaps, using tooling and frameworks built by SDETs.
  • Cross-functional planning: Partner with product managers, developers, and SDETs to translate acceptance criteria into concrete test scenarios, and proactively call out coverage gaps and edge cases.
  • Release quality: Own regression testing for your assigned area ahead of each release, and support the team's release-readiness process.
  • UAT: Help formalize and run User Acceptance Testing across product and engineering as zerohash standardizes this process company-wide.
  • Defect management: Log, triage, and track defects with clear repro steps, severity, and expected-vs-actual detail; follow issues through to resolution.
  • Automation collaboration: Flag coverage gaps that need deeper automated testing and route them to developers, who own unit and integration test automation.
  • Environments: Test across dev, cert, and prod environments, and participate in release readiness reviews.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of QA or test engineering experience, ideally in fintech, payments, or another regulated, API-driven environment.
  • Strong grasp of QA process across all phases of the SDLC: test planning, test data setup, execution, defect management, and release sign-off.
  • Strong test case design and exploratory testing instincts; comfortable reading API specs and testing REST/JSON APIs directly (e.g., Postman, cURL).
  • Experience with BDD-style test scenario writing (Gherkin/Cucumber or similar).
  • Comfortable writing and maintaining automated tests (e.g., Playwright, Selenium) for occasional ad hoc work and automation tech debt.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming or scripting language used for test automation (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript or Python).
  • Working knowledge of SQL for data verification and familiarity with Git-based workflows (GitHub).
  • Experience using Jira and Confluence, or equivalent tools, for test planning, tracking, and documentation.
  • Experience with a test management or UAT tool (e.g., TestRail, Zephyr, or similar).
  • Clear, detailed written communication: bug reports and test plans that others can act on without back-and-forth.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, switching between competing priorities and projects.
  • Comfortable collaborating across time zones with a distributed engineering team.

Preferred

  • Experience testing financial transaction flows: ledgers, settlement, reconciliation, or payments.
  • Exposure to CI/CD pipelines and how automated tests fit into them.
  • Experience working in an Agile/Scrum environment (sprint planning, backlog grooming).

About zerohash

zerohash is the leading crypto and stablecoin infrastructure platform and the operating system for digital money, powering the next generation of financial services. Founded in 2017, zerohash enables banks, brokerages, fintechs, and payment companies to offer crypto trading, stablecoin payments, and tokenized assets without having to build or manage complex blockchain infrastructure on their own.

The zerohash platform supports three core pillars: Trade, Transact, and Tokenize. Through a single integration, customers can launch regulated crypto buy, sell, and custody services; enable 24/7 stablecoin-based funding, payouts, and settlement; and issue and manage tokenized assets with built-in compliance, risk controls, and reporting. By abstracting away technical, regulatory, and operational complexity, zerohash allows partners to treat digital assets as just another financial primitive: fast, programmable, and global.

zerohash is trusted by some of the world’s most recognized financial and consumer brands, including Interactive Brokers, Morgan Stanley, Stripe, Franklin Templeton, BlackRock, DraftKings, Gusto, Worldpay, Kalshi, One Pay, among others. Today, zero infrastructure supports millions of end users across brokerage, wealth, payments, and marketplace platforms globally.

The company is deeply regulated and compliance-first, operating across the U.S. and internationally with licenses and approvals that allow partners to enter crypto and stablecoins with confidence. zerohash has become a trusted partner for enterprises seeking to modernize financial products while meeting the highest standards for security, risk management, and regulatory oversight.

To date, zerohash has raised over $280 million in funding from a mix of leading venture firms and strategic investors, including Morgan Stanley, Interactive Brokers, SoFi, Point72 Ventures, Bain Capital Crypto, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and more.

zerohash has been featured in top-tier media outlets such as Bloomberg, CNBC, The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, Reuters, Forbes, and CoinDesk, and its leadership team regularly contributes to global conversations on the future of payments, investing, and financial infrastructure.

At zerohash, we're building the infrastructure that makes digital money work securely, compliantly, and at global scale.

The zerohash Culture

All zerohash employees are guided by the following characteristics and core principles:

  • Transparency - We believe that transparency is critical to empowering everyone to make the best decisions, both the company to its people and vice versa.

jobs.excerpt: Maybe you call yourself an Internal Communications Manager, a Content Strategist, a Wordsmith-for-Hire, a Chief "Let-Me-Just-Rewrite-That"… or maybe you just call yourself Alex.
jobs.description:
Maybe you call yourself an Internal Communications Manager, a Content Strategist, a Wordsmith-for-Hire, a Chief "Let-Me-Just-Rewrite-That"… or maybe you just call yourself Alex. Whatever title you use, you're the person who takes a messy, half-formed brief and turns it into something people actually want to read, watch, or click through.

What you get

  • €68,000–€78,000 gross per year, based on your experience.
  • €5,000 a year for your own growth, with a real say in how you spend it.
  • 25 vacation days + the option to buy up to 10 more + local public holidays + the option of a sabbatical up to 4 months.
  • Two trips abroad a year with the whole team + occasional drinks and team outings.
  • €500 home-office budget and a great laptop.
  • A well-earned “Hey, well done Buddy!”, now and then.
  • Fully remote, from anywhere in the Netherlands.

Benefits across Europe: the perks above are AYBI’s and go to everyone, everywhere. Statutory benefits (pension, health, social security, leave, sick pay, notice) follow the hire’s country via their local contract or EOR.

About us

All Your BI is a remote-first data agency based in Rotterdam. Since 2019 we’ve grown from a boutique consultancy into an international data team of more than 60 data heroes spread across Europe. We deliver managed BI services for logistics and industrial companies, helping reduce data waste and move businesses forward. We live for the WOW moment, that sparkle in users’ eyes when they gain new insights and discover opportunities. We work according to Holacracy: little hierarchy, lots of ownership. Serious work. Serious fun.

What the job looks like

  • Own our internal communication voice. Company-wide updates, Town Halls and everything in between should sound like All Your BI, not corporate filler.
  • Take a messy, half-formed brief and turn it into a message people actually read: the right words, the right structure, the right length.
  • Build our change muscle by thinking beyond the announcement. What do people need to understand? Where are they likely to get stuck? What actually helps a change land?
  • Own the communication side of change initiatives end to end, building whatever mix of messages, presentations, videos, guides and FAQs the moment calls for.
  • Design and help deliver our Town Halls. Pull together input from across the company, shape the story, build the presentation, prep the presenters, and run the session.
  • Create and coordinate our company-wide communications, keeping our remote, distributed team informed and connected.
  • Keep our People Handbook and other Confluence spaces genuinely easy to use, and help other teams do the same in their own spaces.
  • Take someone else's complex or messy information and turn it into a presentation that's actually clear and easy to follow.
  • Pick the right format for the moment. Sometimes that's a two-minute video, sometimes five slides, sometimes a live session, and sometimes it's deciding we don't need another communication at all.
  • Track how communication is landing and use what you learn to make the next one better.
  • Occasionally help design a learning experience alongside our P&C Lead, and turn a subject-matter expert's know-how into something others can use.
  • Provide some L&D support: keeping tabs on certifications and helping maintain our Udemy setup.

Requirements

What you bring

  • A genuine wordsmith: fluency in English at the level where you catch tone, subtext and register instinctively, not just vocabulary and grammar. You can tighten, restructure, and simplify without losing what the sentence was actually trying to say.
  • Content creation, not just copy: confident building the visual side too — presentations, video edits, and similar — using whatever tools get you there fast, AI included.
  • A good eye: you can spot when something is confusing, too long, visually messy, or unnecessarily corporate, and you know how to fix it.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: you can take a rough brief, ask the right questions, and build something real without needing everything spelled out first.
  • Ownership: you manage your own pieces of work end to end and get things over the line without much hand-holding.
  • Collaborative: you’ll own a lot, but very little of it will be created in isolation.

We’re a growing team across Europe, and we hire to widen that mix, not narrow it. What matters is what you can do and the perspective you bring, not your age, gender, ethnicity, orientation, disability, background, or where you studied. If the role excites you and you bring most of it, apply: the people who add the most rarely tick every box.

Highlights

You'll turn messy briefs into internal comms and content people actually read: Town Halls, change stories, videos and decks for a remote-first team across Europe.

  • Create highly polished, dimensional UI with a strong sense of depth, lighting, materials, contrast, composition, and visual hierarchy.
  • Work confidently with typography and advanced text treatments, including dimensional lettering, gradients, bevels, shadows, highlights, glows, and premium title treatments.
  • Create convincing luxury materials and effects such as gold, polished metal, glass, gems, glossy surfaces, reflections, illumination, glow, and rich decorative details.
  • Maintain excellent readability and usability even within visually rich and highly detailed casino compositions.
  • Explore visual solutions quickly and turn concepts into high-quality, production-ready assets within project timelines.
  • Collaborate closely with the Art Director, Game Designers, Product, and Development teams, while taking ownership of UI quality and visual execution.

  • Strong experience in mobile games, ideally social casino, slots, casino, or other highly polished game products.
  • Excellent command of Adobe Photoshop and professional 2D art workflows.
  • Exceptional skills in typography and text effects, with the ability to create expressive, highly polished game titles and messaging.
  • Strong icon design and rendering skills, including clear silhouettes, dimensionality, material definition, and premium finish.

jobs.excerpt: ABOUT VICTORY LIVE Victory Live is a private equity backed technology company aimed at maximizing distribution and yield for live event ticket inventory.
jobs.description:
ABOUT VICTORY LIVE
Victory Live is a private equity backed technology company aimed at maximizing distribution and yield for live event ticket inventory. We provide an end-to-end software platform for the live ticketing industry, managing thousands of sports, theater, and live music event tickets on behalf of artists, promoters, teams, venues, and professional resellers. Victory Live’s comprehensive offerings include an established B2B marketplace, along with both a full-service and an automated SaaS platform to handle all elements of the ticket sales lifecycle, from ingestion to sales fulfillment.

THE POSITION
Victory Live is looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a team of engineers working across our Ruby, Python, and .NET services. This isn't a pure people-manager role. You'll bring real technical depth, help set architectural direction, and be the person your team looks to when there's no clear answer. You'll also think ahead: understand where your domain needs to go, make the bets, and connect that strategy to your team's day-to-day work.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead and mentor your team, holding a bar for technical excellence, delivery, and stakeholder satisfaction across the engineers who report to you.
  • Set technical direction. Guide architecture and technology decisions for your team's systems, working across Ruby, Python, and .NET as the work requires.
  • Stay hands-on. Spend roughly 5–10% of your time in code reviews, architectural guidance, and hands-on debugging during critical incidents.
  • Translate strategy into execution. Define where your domain needs to be in 12–24 months, turn that into team bets and priorities, and own that narrative with stakeholders.
  • Partner cross-functionally. Align technical strategy with product, business, and other engineering teams, and turn high-level vision into actionable plans.
  • Build the team. Hire, develop, and retain engineers, and create a culture where people do their best work and grow.
  • Drive AI-native practices. Model and push adoption of Claude Code, Copilot, and agentic workflows as a standard part of how your team ships.
  • Own delivery. Plan capacity, manage tradeoffs, and negotiate scope with stakeholders without compromising quality or team health.

REQUIREMENTS

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience across production systems.
  • 3+ years of engineering management experience, with a track record of shipping business-impactful work.
  • Demonstrated ability to set technical strategy and connect it to team execution, not just manage delivery.
  • Strong technical depth in at least one of our core stacks (Ruby on Rails, Python/FastAPI, or C#/.NET), with the ability to speak credibly across the others.
  • Proven ability to attract, retain, and develop engineering talent.
  • Active, deliberate use of AI-powered development tools, with a track record of driving adoption on a team.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to build trust across engineering and non-engineering stakeholders.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience managing distributed teams across onshore and offshore locations.
  • Background in ticketing, marketplaces, e-commerce, or other high-transaction consumer platforms.
  • Experience leading a team through an acquisition, platform consolidation, or major system migration.

WHY VICTORY LIVE

  • You'll build the infrastructure live events run on; millions of tickets, hundreds of venues, many of the largest teams and events in the world.
  • A lean team where decisions move fast and your code reaches real fans, often the same week.
  • Every release has stakes. Every improvement is felt.
  • High expectations, low tolerance for politics, and a culture built on writing well and shipping with care.

OUR VALUES

We build the systems that power live event ticketing, and we hold a high bar for how we do it. Four principles run through everything:

  • Quality of life. Sustainable processes over heroics. Nobody should be a single point of failure, and nobody should be afraid to take a vacation.
  • Quality of code. Clarity over cleverness. If a teammate needs a long explanation to follow your code, it needs simplifying. Tests prove your work; they aren't optional.
  • Protection of production. Every change is reviewed, tested, and observable. We build with monitoring in mind from day one so we find problems before our users do.
  • Shared knowledge. We work across time zones, so we communicate in the open. Questions go in channels, not DMs, and one answer becomes shared knowledge.

ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES
We are an AI-native engineering team. Here is what that looks like in practice:

  • AI-assisted engineering. Every engineer uses Claude, Claude Code, Copilot, and agentic tooling as a routine part of their workflow.
  • Async-first. Most decisions happen in writing through Jira, Confluence, PR descriptions, design docs. We over-communicate on changes and under-communicate on noise.
  • Ownership mindset. Engineers are responsible for what they write and no code reaches production without review. Reviewers are co-owners.
  • Observability is part of "done." If the on-call engineer can't understand a system without reading source, more logging, metrics, and dashboards are needed.
  • Preservation of quality of code and life. We write code that is clean, tested, and maintainable so it serves us well over time, and we build sustainable processes so no one burns out or becomes a single point of failure.
  • Shared knowledge and continued education. We grow as a team by learning from each other through reviews, documentation, and collaboration.

OUR STACK & WAYS OF WORKING

  • VL1 (our core platform), B2B marketplace, distribution integrations, partner-facing APIs
  • Web & mobile clients, REST APIs, microservices
  • Languages: Ruby, Python, Typescript, C-Sharp
  • Frameworks and Technologies: Rails, Hanami, FastAPI, .NET, Postgres, DynamoDB, MSSQL Server, Docker, Terraform
  • Cloud Providers: AWS, Azure
  • Data: Snowflake, dbt, Dagster, AWS, Azure Data Factory, Sigma, Airflow
  • AI tooling: Anthropic / Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, in-house agentic workflows
  • Observability: Datadog, Grafana, Elastic/Kibana, OpsGenie
  • Collaboration: Jira, Confluence, GitHub, Slack, Miro
  • Async-first, agile cadences, distributed onshore + offshore teams

BENEFITS & PERKS

  • Comprehensive medical coverage
  • 100% employer-paid dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid parental leave
  • Paid time off and company holidays
  • Employee wellness and professional development opportunities

Victory Live is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, creed, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, Veteran status, or another other characteristic protected by state, local or federal law.
